complex: IFIT1-IFIT2-IFIT3 interferon-induced complex; functions alongside RIG-I/MDA5 sensing
cancer_dependency_claims: Not a cancer dependency (interferon-inducible effector; loss does not impair proliferation). Its relevance to a DepMap analysis is as an interpretive partner: IFIT1 is the main cellular decoder that makes CMTR1 loss costly, so CMTR1-dependent phenotypes should be IFIT1/IFN-dependent. Strong candidate for an interferon-high-tumour context, analogous to ADAR1.
key_refs: Daffis S 2010 Nature - 2'-O-methylation of the viral mRNA cap evades host restriction by IFIT family members || Habjan M 2013 PLoS Pathog - sequestration of non-2'-O-methylated capped RNA by IFIT1 as a mechanism of translational control || PMID:42043228 - decoding self vs non-self: Cap0 recognition and immune evasion (Viruses 2026)
notes: An inverse reader: IFIT1 binds cap0 (unmethylated at the 2'-O position of N1) and is repelled by the cap1 Nm mark, so its binding is strictly mark-dependent - which satisfies the reader definition with reversed polarity. I know of no positive-sense Nm reader in humans; this is the closest thing to an Nm decoder, and it should be labelled as such in the catalog. || [review] IFIT1 cap0-vs-cap1 discrimination requires IFIT3 (added as reader-cofactor).

complex: IFIT1-IFIT3 heterodimer (IFIT3 C-terminal YxxxL motif); IFIT2-IFIT3 heterodimer also forms and associates with IFIT1
cancer_dependency_claims: Not a cancer dependency - an interferon-inducible effector. DepMap NextGen (local table): Non-dependency, 0/147 NextGen and 0/108 organoid dependent lines (IFIT1 itself is Weakly Selective, 1/147). Its value in this project is identical to the role the curator assigned IFIT1: the cellular decoder that makes cap1 2'-O-methylation (CMTR1) matter, so CMTR1-dependent phenotypes should be IFIT1/IFIT3/IFN-dependent.
key_refs: PMID:29525521 - Johnson 2018 Immunity: crystal structure of cap0-RNA bound to IFIT1 with the IFIT3 C-terminal domain; IFIT3 extends IFIT1 half-life AND allosterically sharpens its specificity for cap0 over cap1/5'ppp RNA || PMID:29554348 - Fleith 2018 Nucleic Acids Res: IFIT3 and IFIT2/3 promote IFIT1-mediated translation inhibition by enhancing binding to non-self (cap0) RNA
notes: The Nm/cap curator kept IFIT1 as the (inverse) cap1-Nm reader but did not consider IFIT3, which two independent laboratories show is required for IFIT1's mark discrimination itself - not merely for its abundance. That is exactly the reader-cofactor definition (cf. MEIOC for YTHDC2, NCBP1 for NCBP2, both already in the union). Species caveat worth recording: mouse Ifit3 lacks the relevant C-terminal domain, so mouse data do not transfer.

complex: Pol II CTD-associated; functionally coupled to RNMT and stimulated by the helicase DHX15
cancer_dependency_claims: CMTR1 is upregulated at mRNA, protein and phosphoprotein level across TCGA/CPTAC tumour types; CRISPR knockout or knockdown suppresses growth of basal-like breast cancer in vitro and in vivo, acting largely through 5'TOP/ribosomal-protein mRNAs, and small-molecule CMTR1 inhibitors have been proposed (Cell Commun Signal 2025). A separate study reports CMTR1 promoting colorectal cancer growth and immune evasion via STAT3, with knockdown improving anti-PD1 efficacy. A CMTR1-ALK fusion has been described in a crizotinib-refractory patient. Expect a broad dependency in CRISPR screens given its role in cap maturation.
key_refs: PMID:20713356 - characterisation of hMTr1, the human cap1 2'-O-ribose methyltransferase (J Biol Chem 2010) || PMID:37024465 - CMTR1 promotes colorectal cancer growth and immune evasion by regulating STAT3 (Cell Death Dis 2023) || PMID:40275371 - multi-omics shows CMTR1 upregulation in cancer and roles in ribosomal protein gene expression and tumour growth (Cell Commun Signal 2025)
notes: Installs the cap1 2'-O-methyl on the first transcribed nucleotide; this is the mark that makes mRNA 'self' to IFIT1 and RIG-I, so CMTR1 loss has a built-in innate-immune/immunotherapy angle. One of the strongest translational candidates in this family and chemically tractable.

complex: None obligate described
cancer_dependency_claims: No substantive cancer-dependency claim; cap2 function remains poorly understood and most CMTR2 literature is incidental (expression correlations). Expected non-essential - a useful contrast to CMTR1 if the new DepMap shows CMTR1 selectivity.
key_refs: Smietanski M 2014 Nat Commun - structural analysis of human cap MTase/CMTR specificity || Werner M 2011 Nucleic Acids Res - 2'-O-ribose methylation of cap2 in human mRNA is catalysed by FTSJD1/CMTR2
notes: Acts only on cap1-methylated substrates (sequential with CMTR1), so an epistatic CMTR1/CMTR2 comparison in DepMap is informative: a CMTR1-only dependency argues for cap1 Nm specifically rather than general cap maturation.

complex: Box C/D snoRNP catalytic core: FBL + NOP56 + NOP58 + SNU13, guided by SNORD box C/D guide RNAs; U6 snRNA Nm additionally requires LARP7
cancer_dependency_claims: p53 represses FBL; FBL overexpression in breast cancer remodels rRNA 2'-O-Me patterns and increases IRES-dependent translation of IGF1R/MYC, and associates with poor outcome (Marcel 2013 Cancer Cell). A 3,275-tumour breast series showed a bimodal effect, with ~10% of tumours having very low FBL that also predicted poor outcome. Widely reported as pan-essential in CRISPR screens (DepMap common essential), so a hit here is largely a ribosome-biogenesis/proliferation confounder rather than evidence of an epitranscriptomic dependency.
key_refs: PMID:24029231 - p53 safeguards translational control by regulating fibrillarin and rRNA methylation in cancer (Cancer Cell 2013) || PMID:28904332 - systematic mapping of 2'-O-Me vulnerability in human rRNA (Sci Rep 2017) || PMID:35545761 - low FBL is an independent marker of poor outcome in breast cancer (BMC Cancer 2022)
notes: Sole catalytic 2'-O-MTase of the human box C/D snoRNP; installs >100 rRNA Nm sites plus snRNA/snoRNA Nm. No validated Nm eraser exists in humans, so Nm writers are the only tractable nodes in this family. For a DepMap analysis, FBL/NOP56/NOP58/SNU13 should be analysed as a module and interpreted against a general ribosome-biogenesis essentiality baseline.

complex: Reported to form a FBL-like box C/D-type RNP; partner composition not fully defined
cancer_dependency_claims: No credible cancer-dependency data; a 2026 review groups FBL and FBLL1 together as candidate ribosome-biogenesis factors in cancer progression but offers no loss-of-function evidence for FBLL1. Expected non-essential in most DepMap lines given its neuron-restricted expression - a plausible 'low-expression, low-dependency' negative control.
key_refs: PMID:39570315 - identification of FBLL1 as a neuron-specific RNA 2'-O-methyltransferase mediating neuronal differentiation (PNAS 2024) || PMID:41524825 - fibrillarin and fibrillarin-like in cancer progression, review (Mol Biol Rep 2026)
notes: FBL paralogue; catalytic activity demonstrated essentially by one lab (2024) in a neuronal context, hence 'proposed'. Expression is highly tissue-restricted, so in DepMap it will mostly be an unexpressed gene - check expression before interpreting any score.

complex: FTSJ1-THADA (Trm732-type, Cm32) and FTSJ1-WDR6 (Trm734-type, Nm34) heterodimers | FTSJ1-WDR6 (Gm34 activity) and FTSJ1-THADA (Cm32 activity); orthologous to yeast Trm7-Trm734 / Trm7-Trm732
cancer_dependency_claims: Loss-of-function causes X-linked intellectual disability and codon-specific translation defects, which is the best-supported phenotype; cancer claims are thinner. Scattered reports propose FTSJ1 as a tumour suppressor or dependency in lung cancer via anticodon-loop Nm and altered translation, but these are single-lab and should be treated as unconfirmed. Not expected to be a common essential. || No cancer-dependency claim; FTSJ1 is an X-linked intellectual-disability gene. Ftsj1-knockout mice lose 2'-O-methylation of 11 cytosolic tRNA species at the anticodon, destabilise tRNA-Phe in brain and show codon-specific translational slow-down with synaptic and behavioural deficits. DepMap: non-dependency.
key_refs: Guy MP & Phizicky EM 2015 RNA - conserved Trm7/Trm732/Trm734 circuit for anticodon-loop Nm || PMID:25404562 - conservation of the Trm7-Trm732/Trm734 circuit; human FTSJ1 and THADA complement yeast mutants || PMID:26310293 - FTSJ1 loss-of-function patient cells lack Cm32 and Gm34 in tRNA-Phe and have reduced o2yW37 || PMID:31019095 - tRNA 2'-O-methylation suppresses endosomal TLR activation (RNA 2019) || PMID:33771871 - Ftsj1 KO mice lose anticodon 2'-O-methylation on 11 tRNAs, with codon-specific translation defects in brain || PMID:33771871 - loss of Ftsj1 perturbs codon-specific translation efficiency in brain, linked to X-linked intellectual disability (Sci Adv 2021)
notes: Installs Cm32 and Gm34 (Nm32/Nm34) in the anticodon loop of tRNA-Phe, tRNA-Trp and tRNA-Leu; Nm34 of tRNA-Phe is a prerequisite for downstream wybutosine (yW) synthesis, so FTSJ1 loss also collapses the yW pathway - relevant if the parent analysis also covers TYW genes. || Included because the anticodon-loop Nm set includes Um32/Um34 on several tRNAs (Nm writer in the Um scope). Note FTSJ1 is distinct from the cap MTase CMTR1. NextGen DepMap: Non-dependency, 0 dependent lines.

complex: Pre-ribosome-associated (with NIP7, DDX52/Rok1-like partners); recruited to HIV-1 RNA via TRBP
cancer_dependency_claims: FTSJ3 is reported to restrain the type I interferon pathway and thereby promote hepatocellular carcinoma immune evasion, with FTSJ3 depletion increasing IFN signalling and immune control (Cancer Res 2024). Independently, as an essential pre-rRNA processing factor it behaves as a broad CRISPR dependency, so DepMap signal is expected to be largely non-selective.
key_refs: PMID:30626973 - FTSJ3 is an RNA 2'-O-methyltransferase recruited by HIV to avoid innate immune sensing (Nature 2019) || PMID:37963197 - RNA methyltransferase FTSJ3 regulates the type I interferon pathway to promote HCC immune evasion (Cancer Res 2024)
notes: Yeast orthologue Spb1 methylates the 25S rRNA A-loop; human FTSJ3 has demonstrated 2'-O-MTase activity and also an essential, methylation-independent role in pre-rRNA processing (its KsgA/FtsJ-dead mutant still supports some processing). Separate catalysis from biogenesis before claiming an Nm-driven dependency.

complex: Functions downstream of PIWI proteins in piRNA biogenesis
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer-dependency claim; HENMT1 loss causes male infertility through piRNA destabilisation and transposon de-repression, and human HENMT1 variants cause spermatogenic failure. Germline/testis-restricted expression means it should be unexpressed and non-scoring in nearly all DepMap lines (possible exception: germ-cell tumour lines, worth a targeted look).
key_refs: PMID:26496356 - HENMT1 and piRNA stability are required for adult male germ cell transposon repression and the spermatogenic program (PLoS Genet 2015) || PMID:31996847 - Zucchini consensus motifs determine the mechanism of pre-piRNA production (Nature 2020)
notes: Installs the 3'-terminal nucleotide 2'-O-methyl on piRNAs (HEN1/HENMT1 is the metazoan small-RNA 2'-O-MTase). This is a terminal-ribose mark, not an internal Nm - worth distinguishing in the catalog. Substrate class 'piRNA' is not in the schema's list, so recorded as miRNA/other.

complex: None obligate described; acts on the mt-LSU 16S rRNA | Standalone SpoU/RlmB-family 2'-O-methyltransferase; Gm1145 of 16S mt-rRNA
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer-dependency claim. Mitochondrial translation genes are usually non-essential in standard glucose-rich DepMap media, so a hit here would be notable and should be checked against OXPHOS-dependency signatures (e.g. in leukaemia models). || None. DepMap (this project): median +0.02, 0.7% of models < -0.5.
key_refs: Lee KW & Bogenhagen DF 2014 J Biol Chem - assignment of the three human mitochondrial 16S rRNA 2'-O-methyltransferases MRM1/MRM2/MRM3 || PMID:25009282 - Rorbach 2014 Mol Biol Cell, MRM2 and MRM3 in mt-LSU biogenesis (MRM1 context) || PMID:25074936 - Lee 2014 JBC, assignment of 2'-O-methyltransferases to sites on mammalian 16S mt-rRNA
notes: Installs Gm1145 of mt-16S rRNA. Together with MRM2 and MRM3 this is a clean, mitochondria-restricted Nm module - a good internal control set because its biology is independent of the nucleolar snoRNP. || Of the three mitochondrial rRNA 2'-O-MTases, MRM1 loss is the best tolerated; human knockouts retain near-normal mitoribosome assembly.

complex: Standalone FtsJ/RrmJ-family 2'-O-methyltransferase; Um1369 (A-loop) of 16S mt-rRNA | mt-LSU assembly intermediate (acts with MRM3 on 16S rRNA) | stand-alone FtsJ/RlmE-family 2'-O-MTase; acts interdependently with MRM3
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer-dependency claim; the strong human phenotype is recessive MRM2 mutation causing a MELAS-like mitochondrial encephalopathy with complex I deficiency. Expected non-essential in standard DepMap conditions. || No cancer-dependency claim. MRM2 controls mitochondrial respiration by gating a late mt-LSU assembly checkpoint; notably this role does NOT require its methyltransferase activity, so a DepMap effect would not be a 2'-O-methylation phenotype. Loss causes a MELAS-like mitochondrial disease and developmental arrest in Drosophila. || Older FTSJ2-era work claimed FTSJ2 suppresses invasion/migration and is upregulated by miR-542-3p as a tumour suppressor in NSCLC - i.e. loss-of-function direction, pre-dating its identification as the mitochondrial A-loop methyltransferase. DepMap (this project): median -0.20, 19% of models < -0.5 (tail to -1.75) - the most essential of MRM1/2/3.
key_refs: Garone C 2017 EMBO Mol Med - MRM2 mutation causes MELAS-like mitochondrial disease || Lee KW & Bogenhagen DF 2014 J Biol Chem - MRM2 makes Um1369 of mt-16S rRNA || PMID:24595062 - Lai 2014 PLoS One, FTSJ2 suppresses cell invasion and migration || PMID:25009282 - MRM2 and MRM3 are involved in biogenesis of the large subunit of the mitochondrial ribosome (Mol Biol Cell 2014) || PMID:25009282 - Rorbach 2014 Mol Biol Cell, MRM2 and MRM3 are required for mt-LSU biogenesis || PMID:28973171 - Garone 2017 Hum Mol Genet, defective MRM2 causes a MELAS-like syndrome || PMID:35177605 - mitochondrial 2'-O-methylation is limited to 16S mt-rRNA (MRM1/MRM2/MRM3); MRM2 gates mt-LSU assembly independently of its catalytic activity
notes: Human orthologue of bacterial RlmE/FtsJ; Um1369 is the mitochondrial equivalent of the bacterial A-loop Um2552. Old symbol FTSJ2 is still common in older papers and some annotation files. || Included as the Um writer of 16S mt-rRNA (MRM1 and MRM3 methylate guanosines and are therefore excluded from this U-centred scope). NextGen DepMap: High Variance, 51/147 dependent lines - a candidate for variance/lineage analysis. || Current symbol MRM2 (renamed from FTSJ2 in 2016) - cancer literature is indexed under FTSJ2, a classic gene-list trap. Human disease gene (MELAS-like, dystonia).

complex: Standalone SpoU-family 2'-O-methyltransferase; Gm1370 of 16S mt-rRNA | mt-LSU assembly intermediate (acts with MRM2 on 16S rRNA)
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer-dependency claim. Depletion impairs mt-LSU biogenesis and mitochondrial translation; interpret any DepMap hit as OXPHOS dependency rather than epitranscriptomic regulation. || None (only a 2002 promoter-characterization paper noting its 17p13.3 location). DepMap (this project): median 0.00, 5% of models < -0.5.
key_refs: Lee KW & Bogenhagen DF 2014 J Biol Chem - MRM3 makes Gm1370 of mt-16S rRNA || PMID:25009282 - MRM2 and MRM3 are involved in biogenesis of the large subunit of the mitochondrial ribosome (Mol Biol Cell 2014) || PMID:25009282 - Rorbach 2014 Mol Biol Cell, MRM3 in mitochondrial large-subunit biogenesis || PMID:25074936 - Lee 2014 JBC, site assignment of mammalian 16S mt-rRNA 2'-O-methylation
notes: Current HGNC symbol is MRM3; RNMTL1 is the legacy symbol and appears in many DepMap-adjacent annotation files, so symbol mapping matters here. || Current symbol MRM3 (renamed from RNMTL1 in 2016).

complex: No obligate partner described (single large multidomain protein)
cancer_dependency_claims: TARBP1 is reported to be upregulated in hepatocellular carcinoma and to promote HCC progression through Gm18-dependent metabolic reprogramming of glutamine, with knockdown reducing tumour growth (Cell Death Differ 2024). Recent work also proposes TARBP1-deposited 2'-O-methyladenosine in mRNA; treat the mRNA-Am claim as not yet independently replicated. Not expected to be a common essential.
key_refs: PMID:31019095 - tRNA Gm18/2'-O-methylation blunts endosomal TLR7/8 activation (RNA 2019) || PMID:38867004 - the tRNA Gm18 methyltransferase TARBP1 promotes HCC progression via glutamine metabolic reprogramming (Cell Death Differ 2024)
notes: Human Trm3 orthologue, makes Gm18 in the tRNA D-loop; Gm18 is immunologically important because it suppresses TLR7-mediated sensing of tRNA - a plausible tumour-immunity angle. The proposed extension to mRNA 2'-O-methyladenosine is the main uncertainty.

complex: None described
cancer_dependency_claims: No credible claim. PubMed searches returned only incidental mentions (e.g. a whole-exome sequencing survey of primary CNS lymphoma), not functional cancer work. Expected non-essential.
key_refs: PMID:38926963 - incidental TRMT13 mention in a CNS lymphoma exome survey (no functional data) || Wilkinson ML 2007 RNA - yeast Trm13 installs Am4/Cm4 (2'-O-methylation at position 4) in tRNA-Gly(GCC), tRNA-His and tRNA-Pro
notes: Human activity inferred from yeast orthology; the position-4 Nm has not, to my knowledge, been biochemically demonstrated for the human enzyme. Include as a candidate writer, flag the weak evidence.

complex: None described | stand-alone 2'-O-methyltransferase (Trm44 orthologue)
cancer_dependency_claims: None. A PubMed search in this session returned a single paper mentioning TRMT44 at all, and it is an unrelated WGCNA module analysis of recurrent pregnancy loss - i.e. there is effectively no functional or cancer literature for the human gene. Expected non-essential. || No cancer-dependency claim at all; DepMap scores TRMT44 as a non-dependency across lineages.
key_refs: Kotelawala L 2008 RNA - yeast Trm44 is the Um44 tRNA-Ser 2'-O-methyltransferase || PMID:18025252 - identification of yeast Trm44 as the tRNA-Ser Um44 2'-O-methyltransferase, conserved in metazoans and fungi || PMID:22895820 - trm44 hypomodification feeds the rapid tRNA decay pathway (synthetic phenotype with tan1/ac4C12) || PMID:32401299 - the only human TRMT44 mention found (a WGCNA module study, not a functional characterisation)
notes: Assignment to Um44 of tRNA-Ser(CGA) rests entirely on orthology to yeast Trm44; no human biochemistry. I could not re-verify the HGNC previous symbol for TRMT44 in this session, so treat the alias list as incomplete. Good candidate for an 'orphan writer' row in the analysis. || PROPOSED for human: the Um44 activity is established for yeast Trm44 and the human gene is assigned by orthology (no published human biochemical demonstration found in this session). Relevant to the scope as an Um writer. NextGen DepMap: Non-dependency, 0 dependent lines.

complex: 7SK snRNP (with MEPCE, HEXIM1/2, P-TEFb); also tethers box C/D snoRNP activity to U6 snRNA
cancer_dependency_claims: LARP7 has been reported as a tumour suppressor in gastric and breast cancer (loss promoting invasion/metastasis), which is the opposite polarity from most writers here; germline biallelic loss causes Alazami syndrome. Not expected to be a common essential. Any DepMap effect is confounded by its P-TEFb-restraining role.
key_refs: PMID:32017896 - LARP7-mediated U6 snRNA modification ensures splicing fidelity and spermatogenesis in mice (Mol Cell 2020) || PMID:32017898 - the Alazami syndrome-associated protein LARP7 guides U6 snRNA modification and contributes to splicing robustness (Mol Cell 2020)
notes: Two independent 2020 Mol Cell papers established that LARP7 is required for box C/D snoRNP-mediated 2'-O-methylation of U6 snRNA, which is why it belongs in this Nm scope as a writer-cofactor and not only as a 7SK chaperone. Dual role (U6 Nm plus 7SK/P-TEFb) makes it a genuine interpretation hazard.

complex: Box C/D snoRNP core (with FBL, NOP58, SNU13); also in U3/U8 snoRNP and pre-rRNA processing
cancer_dependency_claims: No well-supported oncogene/tumour-suppressor claim; the main human genetics link is the intronic GGCCTG repeat expansion causing SCA36. Reported as commonly essential in CRISPR screens; depletion causes nucleolar stress and p53 activation, so expect a broad, non-selective dependency.
key_refs: PMID:33367824 - NOPCHAP1/PAQosome route for box C/D snoRNP (NOP58 loading on RUVBL1/2) (Nucleic Acids Res 2021) || Watkins & Bohnsack 2012 WIREs RNA - box C/D snoRNP architecture and function
notes: Non-catalytic but obligate for a functional box C/D RNP in vivo (NOP56 and NOP58 occupy the two asymmetric halves of the RNP). Include as writer-cofactor; do not interpret a dependency as modification-specific without a catalytic-dead FBL rescue.

complex: Box C/D snoRNP core (with FBL, NOP56, SNU13); assembled via R2TP/PAQosome (RUVBL1/2, NOPCHAP1, ZNHIT3/ZNHIT6, NUFIP1)
cancer_dependency_claims: No specific, replicated cancer-dependency claim beyond generic nucleolar/ribosome-biogenesis addiction of proliferating tumour cells. Expected common essential in CRISPR screens.
key_refs: PMID:33367824 - NOPCHAP1 is a PAQosome cofactor that loads NOP58 onto RUVBL1/2 during box C/D snoRNP biogenesis (Nucleic Acids Res 2021)
notes: HGNC symbol is NOP58; beware the confusing historical NOP5/NOL5 naming shared with NOP56 (NOL5A). Required for snoRNP assembly and therefore for all box C/D-guided Nm.

complex: Box C/D snoRNP core (K-turn-binding nucleating subunit); also a core U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP protein
cancer_dependency_claims: No modification-specific cancer claim. Pan-essential in CRISPR screens, but a large part of that essentiality comes from pre-mRNA splicing (tri-snRNP), not from 2'-O-methylation - the single most important confounder in this gene set.
key_refs: Watkins & Bohnsack 2012 WIREs RNA - box C/D snoRNP assembly || Watkins NJ 2000 Cell - 15.5K/SNU13 binds the K-turn of U4 snRNA and of box C/D snoRNAs
notes: Dual-function protein: flag explicitly in any DepMap interpretation. Its dependency cannot be attributed to Nm.

complex: FTSJ1-THADA (human counterpart of yeast Trm7-Trm732) | obligate partner of FTSJ1 for Cm32 (Trm7-Trm732 module)
cancer_dependency_claims: THADA is recurrently rearranged in benign thyroid adenomas (the origin of its name) and is a type-2-diabetes/PCOS GWAS locus; there is no evidence that any of this depends on its tRNA Nm cofactor role, and no cancer dependency claim. Expected non-essential. || No cancer-dependency claim for its tRNA role; THADA is best known as a thyroid-adenoma-associated locus and a metabolic GWAS gene. DepMap: weakly selective/non-dependent.
key_refs: Guy MP & Phizicky EM 2015 RNA - Trm732/THADA orthology for Cm32 || PMID:25404562 - human THADA complements the yeast trm732 deletion by modifying C32 of tRNA-Phe together with Trm7, establishing it as the TRM732 orthologue || PMID:26310293 - FTSJ1-dependent Cm32/Gm34 circuit in human cells (partner specificity) || PMID:35559166 - identification of a Trm732 motif required for 2'-O-methylation of the tRNA anticodon loop by Trm7 (ACS Omega 2022)
notes: Human THADA-FTSJ1 Cm32 activity is inferred mainly from yeast orthology plus interaction data, so tier is 'proposed'. THADA is a large protein with reported unrelated functions (mitochondrial uncoupling, lipid metabolism) - a strong confounder if it scores in DepMap. || Large multidomain protein with substantial non-RNA literature; dependency signals should be interpreted cautiously. NextGen DepMap: Weakly Selective, 1/147 dependent lines.

complex: FTSJ1-WDR6 (human counterpart of yeast Trm7-Trm734) | presumed obligate partner of FTSJ1 for Nm34 (Trm7-Trm734 module)
cancer_dependency_claims: No specific cancer-dependency claim for the Nm function. WDR6 has unrelated reports as a growth-suppressive STK11/LKB1-interacting protein and in insulin signalling; these should not be read as modification-dependent. Not expected to be a common essential. || No cancer-dependency claim; DepMap shows only weak selectivity, with 3D organoids slightly LESS sensitive than 2D.
key_refs: Guy MP & Phizicky EM 2015 RNA - Trm734 is required for Gm34 and the human WDR6 orthologue substitutes || PMID:25404562 - Trm7-Trm734 circuit for Nm34 is conserved in eukaryotes; human partners assigned by complementation/orthology (THADA = Trm732) || PMID:33771871 - Ftsj1-dependent anticodon Nm32/Nm34 in mammals (pathway context) || PMID:38882062 - amino acids in Trm734 required for 2'-O-methylation of the tRNA wobble residue (ACS Omega 2024)
notes: Obligate specificity subunit: FTSJ1 alone cannot make Gm34. Human reconstitution data are limited relative to the yeast work, hence 'established' rather than 'core'. || PROPOSED for human: the WDR6 = Trm734 assignment rests on orthology and yeast complementation rather than direct human biochemistry; WDR6 also has unrelated reported roles (e.g. metabolic signalling). NextGen DepMap: Weakly Selective, 4/147 dependent lines.

complex: No known catalytic complex. Testis-restricted; associates with RNA via a dsRBD plus a degenerate ADAR-like deaminase domain that lacks catalytic residues.
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer dependency claims. ADAD1 is testis-specific; biallelic ADAD1 variants cause human male infertility with abnormal sperm ultrastructure (PMID:36708028), and Adad1-null mice are male-infertile. Its testis-restricted expression gives it cancer-testis-antigen-like behaviour in some tumours, but no proliferation dependency has been reported.
key_refs: PMID:36708028 - Dai 2023 Hum Mol Genet: biallelic ADAD1 and ADAD2 variants in infertile men, impaired spermatogenesis
notes: Catalytically inactive ADAR-family member - included for completeness of the deaminase-domain family, classified 'other' because it neither installs, removes nor demonstrably reads inosine. Expect near-zero expression in nearly all DepMap lines; any dependency score should be treated as noise unless the line is a germ-cell tumour.

complex: No known catalytic complex; a component of the germ-cell intermitochondrial cement/piRNA-adjacent granule compartment in mouse spermatids. Reported to interact with DNAH17.
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer dependency claims. Homozygous ADAD2 missense variants cause human male infertility (PMID:36708028); Adad2-null mice are male-infertile with disrupted spermiogenesis. Testis-restricted expression, so essentially uninformative in standard DepMap panels.
key_refs: PMID:36708028 - Dai 2023 Hum Mol Genet: homozygous ADAD2 p.R461W in infertile men; reduced sperm ADAD2 and DNAH17
notes: Like ADAD1, a catalytically inactive ADAR-domain RNA-binding protein; included for family completeness and classified 'other'. Not a plausible cancer target; include in the catalog mainly so that a family-level enrichment test is not biased by silently dropping non-catalytic members.

complex: No catalytic complex; monomeric. Binds both ssRNA (via an N-terminal arginine-rich R-domain) and dsRNA; acts as a competitive inhibitor of ADAR1/ADAR2 on shared substrates.
cancer_dependency_claims: ADARB2 is reported as an editing-independent regulator in glioblastoma: ADAR3 is elevated in GBM, where it sequesters substrates from ADAR2 (reducing GRIA2 Q/R editing) and additionally supports NF-kB-driven proliferation and survival (Oakes 2017 JBC; Raghava Kurup 2022 J Biol Chem/NAR). Reported knockdown effects are modest and brain-lineage restricted; no broad dependency claim exists.
key_refs: Oakes 2017 J Biol Chem - ADAR3 antagonises ADAR2 editing in glioblastoma || PMID:10836796 - Chen 2000 RNA: hADAR3 has no detectable editing activity on any known substrate, binds ss+dsRNA, inhibits ADAR1/2 in vitro || Raghava Kurup 2022 - editing-independent ADAR3 function in GBM
notes: Included as 'other' rather than 'writer' because it is catalytically dead - HGNC itself names the gene 'adenosine deaminase RNA specific B2 (inactive)'. Arguably a negative regulator / competitive dsRNA-binder of the A-to-I machinery, which is why it belongs in an RWE catalog even though it installs nothing. Expression is largely restricted to postmitotic neurons and brain, so most DepMap lines will not express it - filter on expression before interpreting any dependency score.

complex: No obligate complex. PABPC1 binds hEndoV in an RNA-dependent manner and stimulates both its activity and its affinity for inosine-containing RNA; hEndoV relocalises to cytoplasmic stress granules on arsenite stress, and its activity is inhibited by physiological ATP concentrations.
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer dependency claims. ENDOV is not reported as essential and has no established role in tumour proliferation or survival; interest in it has been in RNA damage/inosine turnover and in bacterial deoxyinosine repair rather than in oncology.
key_refs: PMID:25195743 - Zhang 2014 Acta Crystallogr D: crystal structure of human EndoV as an inosine-specific ribonuclease, hypoxanthine-binding pocket || PMID:27573237 - Nawaz 2016 J Biol Chem: endogenous hEndoV cleaves inosine-RNA not DNA; PABPC1 partner; stress-granule relocalisation; ATP inhibition
notes: Included as a 'reader' because recognition is strictly mark-dependent: a dedicated hypoxanthine-binding pocket reads the inosine base and cleaves the second/third phosphodiester bond 3' of it in ssRNA (the mammalian enzyme, unlike bacterial EndoV, is RNA-specific). It is a mark-dependent nuclease rather than a signalling reader, which is why its tier is 'established' for biochemistry but the in-vivo substrate set remains open - note it does not cleave inosine-containing dsRNA, so bulk Alu hyper-editing is probably not its substrate. The closest thing this family has to an inosine 'eraser' activity, but it destroys the transcript rather than reversing the mark.

complex: Functions as a homodimer; two isoforms from alternative promoters/start sites - IFN-inducible cytoplasmic p150 (contains Zalpha + Zbeta + 3x dsRBD + deaminase) and constitutive nuclear p110. No obligate separate catalytic cofactor. Activity is modulated by DZF-domain proteins (ILF2/ILF3/ZFR/STRBP) and DHX9; functionally antagonises the dsRNA/Z-RNA sensors PKR (EIF2AK2), MDA5 (IFIH1) and ZBP1.
cancer_dependency_claims: ADAR is the archetypal selective (NOT pan-essential) epitranscriptomic dependency: cancer lines with a high interferon-stimulated-gene (ISG) signature, driven by STING-dependent tumour-intrinsic type I/III IFN, die on ADAR depletion, and a genome-wide CRISPR suppressor screen showed the type I IFN pathway and PKR are required for that lethality (PMID:30559422, shRNA across 398 CCLE lines; concordant Achilles/DRIVE analyses, Gannon 2018 Nat Commun). ADAR1 loss also sensitises tumours to PD-1 blockade via PKR/MDA5 dsRNA sensing (PMID:30559380), and ADAR1 is a self-renewal dependency in blast-crisis CML leukaemia stem cells (PMID:27292188) and in relapsed T-ALL leukaemia-initiating cells, where intrinsic MDA5 level sets the magnitude of ADAR1 dependency (PMID:38265938).
key_refs: PMID:30559380 - Ishizuka 2019 Nature: ADAR1 loss overcomes checkpoint-blockade resistance via PKR/MDA5 || PMID:30559422 - Liu 2019 Nat Med: ISG-high lines are selectively sensitive to ADAR loss; IFN pathway + PKR required || PMID:38265938 - Rivera 2024 Cell Rep: ADAR1 in T-ALL LICs; MDA5 level dictates dependency
notes: Highest-priority gene in this family for a DepMap analysis. For the new DepMap, model ADAR dependency against an ISG/dsRNA-sensor covariate (IFIH1, EIF2AK2, ZBP1, DDX58, MAVS, STING1 expression) rather than pan-cancer - the effect is conditional and will be diluted in an unstratified pan-cancer test. Note p150 vs p110: only p150 carries the Zalpha domain, and the Zalpha-dependent editing of inverted Alu repeats is what restrains ZBP1 (PMID:35859175, PMID:35859176); CRISPR knockout hits both isoforms, so a DepMap signal cannot resolve isoform specificity. No eraser of inosine exists - A-to-I is chemically irreversible, so this subfamily has writers and readers only.

complex: Homodimer; inositol hexakisphosphate (IP6) is buried in the deaminase domain as an obligate structural cofactor (shown in the hADAR2 crystal structure). Auto-edits its own pre-mRNA (-1 alternative splice site) as negative feedback.
cancer_dependency_claims: ADARB1 is generally reported as tumour-suppressive rather than as a dependency: GRIA2 Q/R and other ADAR2-specific editing events are reduced in glioblastoma and astrocytoma, and ADAR2 re-expression suppresses glioma cell growth and migration (Galeano 2013 Oncogene; Tomaselli 2015 Genome Biol). Reduced ADARB1 editing is also reported in HCC and in oesophageal/lung cancer. It is not expected to score as a common-essential or strongly selective dependency in CRISPR screens.
key_refs: Galeano 2013 Oncogene - ADAR2 editing loss in astrocytoma/glioblastoma || PMID:12457566 - Schaub & Keller 2002 Biochimie: ADAR/ADAT family review, substrates and mechanism || Tomaselli 2015 Genome Biol - ADAR2 editing of 3'UTRs and glioblastoma
notes: Site-selective editor (GRIA2 Q/R and R/G, HTR2C, CYFIP2, GABRA3, KCNA1 and thousands of Alu/3'UTR sites). Distinct substrate preference from ADAR1 (prefers the 5' neighbour A/U, and edits the GRIA2 Q/R site, which ADAR1 cannot). For DepMap, treat as a likely negative control within the family: a strong proliferation dependency here would be surprising and worth scrutinising for off-target/CN confounding (ADARB1 sits at 21q22, a region of frequent copy-number change).

complex: Monomeric single-subunit enzyme (unlike the heterodimeric ADAT2/ADAT3). Acts upstream of a Trm5-type methyltransferase (TRMT5 in human) that converts I37 to m1I37.
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer dependency claims. ADAT1 is not reported as essential in CRISPR screens and has no established oncogenic or tumour-suppressive role; the I37/m1I37 mark it initiates is restricted to tRNA-Ala, which limits the scope for a proliferation phenotype.
key_refs: Maas, Gerber & Rich 1999 PNAS - cloning and characterisation of human ADAT1/hTad1p, A37 deaminase || PMID:12457566 - Schaub & Keller 2002 Biochimie: ADAT1 generates I37 (3' of the anticodon) in eukaryotic tRNA-Ala
notes: Deaminates A37 of cytoplasmic tRNA-Ala only (position 3' of the anticodon), not the wobble position - a completely different reaction from ADAT2/ADAT3. Human tRNA-Ala carries m1I37, so ADAT1 is the first of two steps; see TRMT5 entry for the second. Good internal negative control for the family in DepMap: a non-essential tRNA-modification writer in the same subfamily as the essential ADAT2/ADAT3.

complex: Obligate heterodimer with ADAT3 (the ADAT complex). ADAT2 carries the single catalytic cytidine-deaminase-fold active site; ADAT3 is catalytically dead but required for activity and for complex stability/nuclear localisation.
cancer_dependency_claims: Not reported as a cancer-selective target, but expected to behave as a broadly required (common-essential-like) gene: I34 is needed at the wobble position of seven to eight cytoplasmic tRNA isoacceptors for decoding of C/U-ending codons, and loss of ADAT activity reduces I34 and destabilises those tRNAs (PMID:40120092). I did not re-verify the current DepMap essentiality classification in this session. There are scattered reports of ADAT2 overexpression correlating with proliferation in breast and liver cancer, but no validated dependency.
key_refs: PMID:12457566 - Schaub & Keller 2002 Biochimie: ADAT2+ADAT3 heterodimer makes I34 at the wobble position || PMID:40120092 - Del-Pozo-Rodriguez 2025 Brain: ADAT2/ADAT3 complex structure, biochemistry, I34 loss and neuronal migration
notes: If this scores as pan-essential in the new DepMap it is a true-positive housekeeping hit, not a cancer-selective vulnerability - interpret accordingly. The right question for ADAT2/ADAT3 is whether a subset of lines is hypersensitive (codon-usage-biased or tRNA-pool-stressed lines), which needs a continuous-score analysis rather than a binary essentiality call. Note the previous HGNC symbol DEADC1, which still appears in older annotation files and will break naive symbol joins.

complex: Monomeric SAM-dependent methyltransferase; no obligate cofactor. Acts downstream of ADAT1 in the m1I37 pathway (ADAT1: A37 -> I37; then N1-methylation -> m1I37). | Standalone Trm5-family methyltransferase; m1G37 in cytosolic and mitochondrial tRNAs (also the committed first step of yW synthesis)
cancer_dependency_claims: TRMT5 is best characterised as a mitochondrial-disease gene (biallelic variants cause combined OXPHOS deficiency via hypomodified mt-tRNAs). Cancer claims are limited and mostly correlative - TRMT5 has been reported as required for growth in hepatocellular carcinoma models - and do not reach the standard of METTL3-in-AML-type evidence. Any DepMap signal would most plausibly reflect its m1G37 activity on cytoplasmic and mitochondrial tRNAs, not m1I37. || TRMT5 is upregulated in HCC and correlates with poor prognosis; silencing attenuated proliferation and metastasis in vitro and in vivo, lowered ECAR/OCR, destabilised HIF-1alpha and sensitised cells to doxorubicin (PMID:36632750). Single-group claim but a concrete, testable HCC dependency. || Strongest non-KEOPS dependency claim in this family. CRISPR synthetic-lethality screens identified TRMT5-dependent m1G37 as required for cytarabine and venetoclax tolerance in AML; the effect maps specifically to its mitochondrial function (mt-mRNA translation/OXPHOS upregulation), and degron-mediated TRMT5 depletion plus cytarabine/venetoclax is synergistic (Pauli 2025 Blood). In HCC, TRMT5 is overexpressed, and silencing reduces proliferation/metastasis and destabilizes HIF-1alpha, sensitizing to doxorubicin (Zhao 2023). DepMap (this project): median -0.52, 54% of models < -0.5, CEGv2 gene.
key_refs: Bjork & Grosjean (yeast Trm5) - Trm5 methylates I37 to m1I37 in tRNA-Ala || PMID:12457566 - Schaub & Keller 2002 Biochimie: the ADAT1 I37 step of the tRNA-Ala m1I37 pathway || PMID:26189817 - Powell 2015 AJHG, TRMT5 mutations cause mt-tRNA modification defect with respiratory-chain deficiency || PMID:26189817 - Powell 2015 Am J Hum Genet: TRMT5 mutations cause mt-tRNA G37 hypomodification and multiple respiratory-chain deficiencies || PMID:36632750 - Zhao 2023 J Zhejiang Univ Sci B, targeting TRMT5 suppresses HCC via HIF-1alpha || PMID:36632750 - Zhao 2023 J Zhejiang Univ Sci B: targeting TRMT5 suppresses HCC progression via the HIF-1alpha pathway || PMID:40749163 - Pauli 2025 Blood, TRMT5-mediated m1G as a mitochondrial vulnerability in drug-resistant AML || Suzuki 2021 Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol - tRNA modification pathways including m1G37/m1I37 assignment
notes: Listed here only because the task asked whether ADAT1's I37 becomes m1I37 via TRMT5 - the answer is: yes in the accepted pathway model, but the enzyme assignment for the human m1I37 step is inferred from yeast/plant Trm5, not demonstrated directly in human cells, hence tier 'proposed'. TRMT5's core, uncontested activity is m1G37, which belongs to the methyltransferase curator's scope - expect and tolerate duplication there, and defer to that entry for the m1G evidence tier (established/core). || m1G37 (and m1I37 on inosine-37 tRNA-Ala) immediately 3' of the anticodon; acts on both mitochondrial and cytosolic tRNAs, with the mitochondrial phenotype dominant in patients. || Dual-compartment and dual-pathway (mt m1G37 plus cytosolic yW precursor). Good candidate for drug-resistance/OXPHOS-context analyses in a larger DepMap, including 3D/organoid models where OXPHOS reliance differs.

complex: Obligate non-catalytic subunit of the ADAT2/ADAT3 heterodimer; its degenerate deaminase-like domain completes the substrate-binding surface and the active-site pocket of ADAT2. ADAT2 has no activity without it.
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer dependency claims. Biallelic hypomorphic ADAT3 variants cause a recessive neurodevelopmental disorder with microcephaly and impaired radial neuronal migration, with phenotype severity tracking the degree of loss of ADAT activity (PMID:40120092) - i.e. partial loss is viable in humans, while complete loss of ADAT function is expected to be cell-lethal. Expected to behave like ADAT2 in CRISPR screens; current DepMap classification not re-verified here.
key_refs: PMID:40120092 - Del-Pozo-Rodriguez 2025 Brain: 21 NDD patients with biallelic ADAT3 variants; ADAT3 is the catalytically inactive subunit; variants reduce complex abundance/activity and I34
notes: A textbook 'writer-cofactor': zero catalytic activity, absolutely required for catalysis. Pairs with ADAT2 as a positive control for the obligate-cofactor class in this catalog (alongside METTL14/WTAP, TRMT112, WDR4 in other families) - if cofactors systematically track their catalytic partners' DepMap profiles, that is a useful internal consistency check on the whole RWE analysis.

complex: Minimal functional 'editosome' = APOBEC1 + one obligate cofactor, either A1CF or RBM47 (and, per a recent report, RBM46). APOBEC1 + A1CF alone reconstitute apoB editing in heterologous cells. Auxiliary/modulatory factors: SYNCRIP (GRY-RBP), HNRNPC, HNRNPA1 (ABBP1), KHSRP (KSRP), CELF2 (CUGBP2).
cancer_dependency_claims: APOBEC1 is oncogenic when ectopically expressed rather than being a dependency: APOBEC1-transgenic mice develop hepatic dysplasia and hepatocellular carcinoma (Yamanaka 1995 PNAS), and APOBEC1-dependent editing has been linked to colorectal and oesophageal tumourigenesis. Expression is tightly tissue-restricted (small intestine, and liver in rodents), so most DepMap lines will not express it and a dependency signal is not expected.
key_refs: PMID:11976346 - Lellek 2002 J Biol Chem: APOBEC1 + ACF/ASP constitute the core apoB mRNA editing enzyme in vivo || PMID:25806564 - Severi & Conticello 2015 RNA Biol: live-cell C>U editing reporter; interplay of APOBEC1 with ACF, hnRNP-C1, GRY-RBP || Yamanaka 1995 PNAS - APOBEC1 transgenic mice develop hepatocellular carcinoma
notes: The one bona fide, uncontested site-specific C-to-U mRNA editing enzyme in humans (APOB C6666 -> UAA stop, giving ApoB48). Gate on expression before interpreting DepMap scores: intestinal/colorectal lines are the only plausible context. Distinguish sharply from the APOBEC3 branch - APOBEC1's RNA activity is core, the APOBEC3 RNA claims are not.

complex: Single-domain zinc-dependent cytidine deaminase; no obligate cofactor identified for the reported RNA activity (in contrast to the APOBEC1 editosome).
cancer_dependency_claims: APOBEC3A matters in cancer as a DNA mutator, not as a dependency: it is the principal source of the APOBEC mutational signatures SBS2/SBS13 across bladder, breast, lung and cervical cancers, and its expression causes replication stress, which underlies proposed synthetic-lethal combinations with ATR/CHK1 inhibition. There is no credible claim that cancer cells depend on APOBEC3A for proliferation, and its RNA-editing function has not been linked to any dependency.
key_refs: PMID:27149507 - Sharma 2016 RNA Biol: transient APOBEC3A overexpression causes C-to-U editing at >4200 sites in 3078 genes || PMID:30791937 - Sharma 2019 Genome Biol: context for the A3A/A3G RNA-editing series (monocytes/macrophages under hypoxia and IFN)
notes: Marked controversial on purpose. The site-specific mRNA C-to-U editing attributed to APOBEC3A comes essentially from one group (Baysal/Sharma), the strongest datasets involve transient overexpression in HEK293T, and the physiological editing levels in primary cells are low and condition-restricted (hypoxia, interferon, pro-inflammatory macrophages). The overwhelmingly better-established substrate for APOBEC3A is single-stranded DNA. Include it in the catalog for completeness but do not let it drive any family-level conclusion; if it scores in DepMap, the DNA-damage/replication-stress interpretation is far more likely than an RNA-mark one.

complex: Two-domain cytidine deaminase (catalytic C-terminal domain); no obligate cofactor identified for the reported RNA activity.
cancer_dependency_claims: Reported to induce widespread site-specific C-to-U mRNA editing in primary NK cells, CD8 T cells and lymphoma cell lines upon cellular crowding/hypoxia or mitochondrial respiratory inhibition, with enrichment for translation/ribosome genes and a Warburg-like metabolic shift in HuT78 cells (PMID:30791937). This is an adaptive-response claim, not a dependency claim; APOBEC3G also contributes to APOBEC mutagenesis in some tumours. No proliferation dependency reported.
key_refs: PMID:30791937 - Sharma 2019 Genome Biol: mitochondrial hypoxic stress induces widespread C-to-U RNA editing by APOBEC3G in NK cells and lymphoma lines
notes: Same caveats as APOBEC3A and from the same group, so the two claims are not independent evidence; its canonical, consensus function is ssDNA deamination of retroviral/retroelement cDNA (anti-HIV-1 restriction). Tier controversial. Expression is largely restricted to lymphoid lineages, which further limits what DepMap can say. Included so the catalog is explicit about which APOBEC3 members have RNA claims and which do not.

complex: Obligate cofactor of APOBEC1 for apoB mRNA editing; three RRM domains plus an auxiliary domain, docks APOBEC1 onto the mooring sequence downstream of the edited C.
cancer_dependency_claims: Hepatocyte A1cf overexpression in mice drives steatosis, fibrosis, dysplasia and spontaneous hepatocellular carcinoma, accelerated by a high-fat/high-fructose diet and - importantly - independent of Apobec1; elevated A1CF in human HCC tissue correlates with advanced fibrosis and reduced survival in NAFLD-associated cases (PMID:33445170). So the oncogenic claim is for A1CF as an RNA-binding protein, not as an editing cofactor. No proliferation dependency reported.
key_refs: PMID:11976346 - Lellek 2002 J Biol Chem: ACF/ASP is the essential second component of the apoB editing enzyme || PMID:33445170 - Blanc 2021 J Clin Invest: hepatic A1CF overexpression causes steatosis, fibrosis and HCC, independent of Apobec1
notes: Genuine obligate writer-cofactor for the APOBEC1 reaction, hence 'core'. But note the dissociation in the cancer literature: the A1CF HCC phenotype is editing-independent and APOBEC1-independent, so A1CF and APOBEC1 are NOT expected to show correlated DepMap profiles - a useful caution against inferring complex membership from co-dependency alone in this family.

complex: Reported third APOBEC1 cofactor, paralogous to A1CF/RBM47 (three RRMs); supports APOBEC1-dependent apoB C-to-U editing in reconstitution assays and defines a partly distinct target set by low-error circular RNA sequencing.
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer dependency claims. RBM46 is germ-cell/testis-enriched (cancer-testis antigen CT68) and functions in mouse germ-cell mRNA stability and piRNA pathway biology; no proliferation dependency or tumour phenotype has been reported.
key_refs: PMID:38708190 - Wang 2023 J Mol Biol: identification and characterisation of RBM46 as a novel APOBEC1 cofactor for C-to-U editing
notes: A genuine 2023 addition to this family - worth including precisely because most published RWE gene lists predate it and therefore omit it. Tier 'proposed': single laboratory, largely reconstitution/overexpression-based, physiological relevance in human tissue not yet established. Testis-restricted expression means near-zero informativeness in DepMap.

complex: Alternative obligate cofactor of APOBEC1, functionally interchangeable with A1CF for apoB C-to-U editing; three RRMs. In mouse intestine RBM47, not A1CF, is the physiologically dominant APOBEC1 partner.
cancer_dependency_claims: RBM47 is a tumour and metastasis SUPPRESSOR, not a dependency: loss of RBM47 is selected during breast cancer progression and promotes metastatic re-initiation and growth, acting through stabilisation of target mRNAs such as DKK1 (PMID:24898756). Similar tumour-suppressive roles are reported in lung and colorectal cancer. Expect depletion-resistant or even growth-promoting CRISPR scores, i.e. a negative control for 'dependency' framing.
key_refs: PMID:24898756 - Vanharanta 2014 eLife: RBM47 loss as a selectable metastatic trait in breast cancer; HITS-CLIP target map || PMID:38708190 - Wang 2023 J Mol Biol: confirms A1CF and RBM47 as the two established APOBEC1 editosome cofactors
notes: Included because it is a bona fide obligate APOBEC1 cofactor, but its cancer biology (tumour suppression via broad mRNA binding) is unrelated to C-to-U editing. Like A1CF, a reminder that in the editing/deamination family the well-documented cancer phenotypes are mostly editing-independent RBP functions - worth stating explicitly when the DepMap results are interpreted.

complex: PABPC1-PAIP1 translational co-activator complex (disrupted by Psi-modified mTOG tRF binding to its RRMs)
cancer_dependency_claims: Guzzi 2022 Nat Cell Biol: Psi-modified mini-tRFs (mTOG-Psi, PUS7-dependent) bind PABPC1 RRM domains, block PAIP1 recruitment and repress aberrant protein synthesis; loss of this axis accompanies leukaemic progression in myelodysplastic syndrome, and PUS7 is the well-known MDS/glioblastoma-stem-cell dependency at the writer end. DepMap NextGen (local table): Pan-dependency, 140/147 NextGen and 104/108 organoid dependent lines (core translation), so the CRISPR signal is not Psi-specific.
key_refs: PMID:35292784 - Guzzi 2022 Nat Cell Biol: pseudouridylated mTOG tRFs target PABPC1 RRM domains (isotope-exchange proteomics), repress aberrant translation and predict leukaemic progression in MDS
notes: IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: the m6A curator excluded PABPC1, correctly, for lack of m6A mark-dependence. That exclusion does not cover Psi, where isotope-exchange proteomics mapped Psi-dependent contacts with its RRMs and defined the downstream mechanism. It is the reader end of the PUS7 axis the catalog already carries, so leaving it out breaks that axis. Pan-essential - interpret as an axis member, not a target.

complex: None; acts with DKC1-installed Psi sites (e.g. TPI1 mRNA)
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer-dependency claim for the Psi-reading function (PFN1 mutations cause ALS; PFN1 is widely studied in cytoskeletal biology and metastasis). DepMap NextGen (local table): Pan-dependency, 123/147 NextGen and 90/108 organoid dependent lines - pan-essential for actin dynamics, so the dependency is not Psi-related.
key_refs: PMID:39812085 - J Am Chem Soc 2024/2025: quantitative proteomics identifies profilin-1 (PFN1) as a pseudouridine-binding protein; PFN1 binds Psi-containing RNA directly and selectively and regulates stability/translation of a DKC1-installed Psi site in TPI1 mRNA
notes: DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS a stated catalog decision: the psi_uridine curator wrote 'No verified human Psi-reader protein was identified in this session - I recommend the catalog carry no Psi reader entries until one is published.' One has been published (JACS, unbiased proteomics plus direct and selective binding plus ~4000 binding sites plus a mechanistic Psi-dependent effect). PFN1, PABPC1 and MYL6 together give the Psi family its missing reader layer.

complex: H/ACA snoRNP/scaRNP core with NOP10, NHP2, GAR1 (+NAF1/SHQ1 assembly); telomerase RNP
cancer_dependency_claims: Dkc1 hypomorphic mice reproduce dyskeratosis congenita and develop tumours, with impaired rRNA pseudouridylation preceding telomere shortening (Ruggero 2003). DKC1 is over-expressed in colorectal, lung, renal, gastric and glial tumours, where knockdown blocks proliferation/migration and induces senescence or apoptosis; in CRC, DKC1 stabilises ribosomal-protein mRNAs and the DKC1 inhibitor pyrazofurin synergises with trametinib in vitro and in vivo. DKC1 is also a near-universal pan-essential gene in DepMap.
key_refs: PMID:12522253 - Dkc1m mice: impaired rRNA pseudouridylation, DC phenotype and tumour susceptibility || PMID:34026451 - DKC1 drives CRC growth; catalytically dead D125A inactive; pyrazofurin + trametinib synergy || PMID:9590285 - DKC1 mutations cause X-linked dyskeratosis congenita; dyskerin carries TruB PUS motifs
notes: Target specificity is snoRNA-guided, so DKC1 loss removes ~100 rRNA Psi sites plus snRNA sites and destabilises TERC. Human 28S Psi is measurably reduced in DC patient ribosomes (PMID:30202881). NextGen DepMap: Pan-dependency, 139/147 dependent lines, common-essential in 2D as well - expect no selectivity, use as a positive control.

complex: SPOUT-class methyltransferase dimer; 18S/SSU processome-associated | nucleolar ribosome-assembly factor (SPOUT-class fold, functions as a dimer)
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer dependency claim. A hypomorphic EMG1 mutation causes Bowen-Conradi syndrome (severe developmental disorder with profound growth failure), implying the gene is essential and dose-sensitive in normal cells - so expect common-essential behaviour with a poor therapeutic window. || No cancer-dependency claim; EMG1 D86G causes Bowen-Conradi syndrome (severe growth failure, psychomotor retardation) through protein destabilisation. DepMap shows a High Variance profile with a marked 3D-organoid preference, which is unexplored in the literature.
key_refs: PMID:19463982 - EMG1 p.D86G mutation causes Bowen-Conradi syndrome || PMID:20047967 - Nep1/EMG1 is a pseudouridine-N1-specific methyltransferase, acting only on Psi-containing substrates || PMID:20047967 - Wurm 2010 NAR: Nep1/EMG1 is the first identified N1-specific pseudouridine methyltransferase, making the m1 of m1acp3Psi in 18S rRNA; activity conserved in human Nep1 || PMID:20972225 - in vivo Nep1/Emg1 catalyses the N1-methylation of Psi1191 (yeast 18S), a dual methyltransferase/assembly-factor role
notes: Installs only the N1-methyl half of the hypermodified m1acp3Psi1248 (human numbering) next to the P-site tRNA; TSR3 adds the acp3 group. The human enzymatic assignment is inferred from conservation plus activity of human Nep1 - solid but not as deeply validated as in archaea/yeast. || Writer of the N1-methyl group of the hypermodified m1acp3Psi1248 in human 18S rRNA - i.e. a genuine Psi-dependent writer, which is why it belongs in this family rather than with generic MTases. NextGen DepMap: High Variance, 39/147 dependent lines; strong 3D>2D difference (-0.416 vs -0.155, FDR=0.026).

complex: Standalone TruA-family pseudouridine synthase (nuclear and mitochondrial pools) | stand-alone (TruA family); no obligate partner
cancer_dependency_claims: PUS1 protein/mRNA is up-regulated in hepatocellular carcinoma and in basal-like breast cancer, where high expression tracks with poor survival; no cell-autonomous dependency has been demonstrated and DepMap classifies it as only weakly selective, so published claims are expression/prognosis-based rather than dependency-based. || Several oncogenic claims: PUS1 promotes HCC by pseudouridylating mRNAs to enhance oncogenic translation (Hu 2024 Hepatology); PUS1 is a poor-prognosis/TNBC biomarker; a non-enzymatic FOXA1-PUS1-EIF3B axis is reported in prostate cancer bone metastasis. Disease biology (MLASA) shows mt-tRNA pseudouridylation governs erythropoiesis, with rapamycin partially rescuing anaemia (Wang 2024 Blood). DepMap (this project): median +0.04, 1.7% of models < -0.5.
key_refs: PMID:15108122 - Bykhovskaya 2004 Am J Hum Genet, PUS1 missense mutation causes MLASA || PMID:15108122 - homozygous PUS1 missense causes MLASA (mitochondrial myopathy + sideroblastic anaemia) || PMID:31477916 - structure-dependent mRNA target recognition by Pus1 (high-throughput kinetics) || PMID:38635773 - Wang 2024 Blood, mitochondrial tRNA pseudouridylation governs erythropoiesis || PMID:41136621 - BACS KO map: PUS1 installs Psi27/28 in cy- and mt-tRNA; integrated stand-alone PUS map || PMID:41136621 - Xu 2025 Nat Cell Biol, comprehensive tRNA Psi map (PUS1 responsible for Psi27/28 and mt Psi20/25/66-68)
notes: Localises to nucleus, cytosol and mitochondria; also responsible for all 8 Psi sites in human mt-mRNA. Patient cells lack Pus1p-dependent tRNA Psi (PMID:15772074). NextGen DepMap (Nature 2026 tables): Weakly Selective, 4/147 dependent lines; 3D organoids slightly more sensitive than 2D (diff -0.08, FDR<0.001). || The major mitochondrial PUS: Psi27/28 in cy- and mt-tRNAs, Psi20/25/66-68 in mt-tRNAs, and all eight mt-mRNA Psi sites. Note the prostate-cancer claim is explicitly catalysis-independent.

complex: stand-alone (Pus10 family); interacts with DROSHA-DGCR8 microprocessor (catalysis-independent)
cancer_dependency_claims: PUS10 depletion reduces mature miRNA levels and accumulates pri-miRNAs in multiple human cell lines, a catalysis-independent activity that would be expected to affect tumour-suppressive miRNA output; Pus10-knockout mice show cell-intrinsic interferon activation and altered tRNA-derived small RNAs, and a PUS10 signature is linked to human autoimmune disease. No direct tumour-dependency experiment has been published.
key_refs: PMID:31819270 - PUS10 promotes miRNA biogenesis via microprocessor binding, independent of catalytic activity; PUS10-dependent tRNA Psi sites mapped || PMID:40402745 - Pus10 loss alters tdRs, activates cGAS-STING/IFN and confers inflammation resistance in vivo || PMID:41136621 - PUS10 catalyses Psi54 (fully) and Psi55 (partially) in cy-tRNA, redundantly with TRUB1
notes: Dual-function gene: catalytic (tRNA Psi54/55) and non-catalytic (miRNA processing); for a DepMap analysis any signal cannot be attributed to Psi alone. NextGen DepMap: Weakly Selective, 3/147 dependent lines.

complex: homodimer; stand-alone (TruA family)
cancer_dependency_claims: No credible cancer-dependency claim; PUS3 is a neurodevelopmental-disease gene (intellectual disability) and is essentially non-dependent across DepMap lines.
key_refs: PMID:27055666 - homozygous truncating PUS3 mutation causes intellectual disability with reduced tRNA Psi38/39 || PMID:38996458 - cryo-EM of PUS3 homodimer bound to tRNA; Pseudo-seq shows no evidence for human PUS3 mRNA targets || PMID:41136621 - PUS3 activity restricted to Psi38-40 of cytosolic tRNAs (not mt-tRNA)
notes: Important negative result: PUS3 does NOT modify mRNA (PMID:38996458) and does NOT modify mt-tRNA (that is PUSL1). NextGen DepMap: Weakly Selective, 1/147 dependent lines.

complex: stand-alone (TruD family)
cancer_dependency_claims: PUS7 is the best-supported Psi cancer dependency: it is over-expressed in glioblastoma, high expression predicts worse survival, and PUS7 expression plus catalytic activity are required for glioblastoma stem-cell tumorigenicity, with small-molecule PUS7 inhibitors suppressing tumour growth and extending survival in mice (Cui 2021 Nat Cancer). A tumour-suppressor gene is the wrong shape for a dependency screen - expect no CRISPR signal (NextGen DepMap: Weakly Selective, 1/147 dependent lines).

complex: 2-thiouridylase acting with the sulfur-relay donor NFS1; acts on U34 of mt-tRNA-Lys/Glu/Gln together with MTO1-GTPBP3 | mitochondrial 2-thiouridylase; acts with MTO1/GTPBP3 on mt-tRNA U34
cancer_dependency_claims: TRMU confers resistance of BRAFV600E melanoma cells to vemurafenib by modulating mitochondrial activity (quantitative-proteomics study of epitranscriptomic drug-resistance regulators), and TRMU appears in an RBP-based bladder-cancer prognostic signature. Biallelic TRMU mutations cause reversible infantile liver failure, establishing strong loss-of-function physiology. || TRMU (with MTO1) is upregulated in vemurafenib-resistant melanoma; TRMU depletion lowers OXPHOS and resensitizes resistant cells to vemurafenib (Guo 2025 J Proteome Res) - a drug-resistance dependency rather than a growth dependency. DepMap (this project): median +0.07, 0.6% of models < -0.5.

notes: ONE OF THE MOST SELECTIVE GENES IN THIS SCOPE: NextGen DepMap Strongly Selective, 21/147 dependent lines (20/108 organoids), and markedly more essential in 3D organoids than matched 2D lines (-0.304 vs -0.049, FDR<0.001) - a strong candidate hit for the 3D/NextGen analysis. Pathological mutants are degraded by CLPP (PMID:38113276). || Cysteine/sulfur supply (NFS1) and the modifier allele burden make TRMU phenotypes conditional (reversible infantile liver failure). Expect context-dependent rather than pan-essential CRISPR behaviour.

complex: cytosolic thiouridylase CTU1-CTU2 heterodimer
cancer_dependency_claims: Same pathway claims as CTU1: over-expression in breast cancer with a requirement for invasion/metastasis, and synthetic lethality with MAPK inhibition in BRAF-mutant melanoma. CTU2 is additionally pan-essential in DepMap, unlike CTU1.
key_refs: PMID:18391219 - Ctu1-Ctu2 complex required for cytosolic tRNA 2-thiolation and genome stability || PMID:27811057 - CTU2 among U34 enzymes sustaining breast cancer metastasis || PMID:29925953 - CTU2 targeting with MAPK inhibitors kills melanoma cells
notes: Asymmetry worth testing: CTU2 is Pan-dependency (104/147 dependent lines) while its obligate partner CTU1 is only weakly selective, which argues CTU2 has thiolation-independent essential roles.

complex: small CSL/zinc-finger electron-donor protein shared between the diphthamide pathway (DPH1/DPH2) and the Elongator/KTI12 pathway
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer-dependency claim specific to its tRNA-modification role. DepMap scores DPH3 as pan-essential, but that essentiality is most plausibly explained by diphthamide biosynthesis on eEF2, so any hit should not be read as a wobble-U phenotype.
key_refs: PMID:30916349 - Kti12/Elongator regulatory axis in which Kti11/DPH3 functions in yeast tRNA anticodon modification || PMID:36617428 - human Elongator biochemistry (context for accessory factors)
notes: PROPOSED/dual-pathway: the Kti11-Elongator connection is established in yeast; direct human evidence that DPH3 is required for mcm5U is lacking. Flagged so the DepMap signal is not over-interpreted. NextGen DepMap: Pan-dependency, 125/147 dependent lines; 3D slightly LESS sensitive than 2D (FDR=0.020).

complex: Elongator: ELP123 (ELP1-ELP2-ELP3) + ELP456 (ELP4-ELP5-ELP6); regulated by KTI12
cancer_dependency_claims: ELP1 is a bona fide cancer-predisposition gene: rare germline loss-of-function ELP1 variants occur in ~14% of paediatric SHH medulloblastoma (the commonest medulloblastoma predisposition gene, raising predisposition prevalence to 40% in that subgroup), with biallelic inactivation via chromosome-9q loss, destabilised Elongator, loss of U34 tRNA modifications, codon-dependent translational reprogramming and UPR induction. ELP1 is also pan-essential in DepMap, and Elongator inhibition has been proposed as a melanoma/breast-cancer strategy together with ELP3/CTU1/CTU2.
key_refs: PMID:25450681 - familial dysautonomia (IKBKAP/ELP1) patient tissues have reduced mcm5s2U || PMID:32296180 - germline ELP1 loss-of-function predisposes to SHH medulloblastoma via Elongator destabilisation and proteome instability || PMID:36617428 - cryo-EM of fully assembled Elongator (yeast/mouse) and biochemistry of human Elongator
notes: Scaffold subunit: obligate non-catalytic partner of ELP3, hence writer-cofactor. NextGen DepMap: Pan-dependency, 126/147 dependent lines (common essential); 3D marginally LESS sensitive than 2D.

complex: Elongator ELP123 subcomplex
cancer_dependency_claims: No gene-specific cancer-dependency claim; ELP2 is required for Elongator integrity and the U34 pathway whose enzymes are up-regulated in breast cancer and required for BRAF-mutant melanoma survival. DepMap shows a High Variance (not pan-essential) profile, making ELP2 an interesting selectivity candidate.
key_refs: PMID:22854966 - Elongator subunit requirements for melanoma migration/tumorigenicity (ELP1/ELP3 and ELP5/ELP6) || PMID:36617428 - architecture of ELP123 and assembly with ELP456; conservation in human Elongator
notes: NextGen DepMap: High Variance, 75/147 dependent lines - among the less uniformly essential Elongator subunits.

complex: Elongator ELP456 hetero-hexamer (RecA-like ATPase fold)
cancer_dependency_claims: No gene-specific dependency claim beyond the Elongator pathway; DepMap classifies ELP4 as High Variance rather than pan-essential.
key_refs: PMID:22854966 - DERP6/ELP5 directly connects ELP3 to ELP4 within human Elongator || PMID:36617428 - structure/function of ELP456 and its association with ELP123
notes: NextGen DepMap: High Variance, 70/147 dependent lines.

complex: Elongator ELP456 hetero-hexamer; bridges ELP3 and ELP4
cancer_dependency_claims: ELP5 (DERP6) depletion phenocopies ELP1/ELP3 loss in melanoma-derived cells, reducing migration, invasion and tumorigenicity - the original evidence that ELP5/ELP6 are functional Elongator subunits with pro-tumour roles. Pan-essential in DepMap.
key_refs: PMID:22854966 - DERP6 (ELP5) and C3ORF75 (ELP6) are human Elongator subunits required for melanoma migration, invasion and tumorigenicity || PMID:36617428 - ELP456 assembly and tRNA-modification activity
notes: NextGen DepMap: Pan-dependency, 144/147 dependent lines - the most essential Elongator subunit in this dataset; 3D more sensitive than 2D (-1.335 vs -1.159, FDR=0.001).

complex: Elongator ELP456 hetero-hexamer
cancer_dependency_claims: As for ELP5: ELP6 (C3ORF75) knockdown reduces melanoma-cell migration, invasion and tumorigenicity, establishing it as a functionally required Elongator subunit. Pan-essential in DepMap, no tumour-selective claim.
key_refs: PMID:22854966 - C3ORF75/ELP6 identified as a human Elongator subunit essential for Elongator function in melanoma cells || PMID:36617428 - cryo-EM architecture of ELP456 within fully assembled Elongator
notes: NextGen DepMap: Pan-dependency, 129/147 dependent lines.

complex: GTPBP3-MTO1 complex (GTPase subunit; GTP-dependent activation of taurinomethyl transfer) | MTO1-GTPBP3 complex (GTPase subunit)
cancer_dependency_claims: No mechanistic cancer-dependency study; GTPBP3 appears as one of three hub RNA-binding proteins in a laryngeal squamous-cell-carcinoma prognostic signature and in pan-cancer RNA-modification-enzyme multi-omics surveys, which are correlative. GTPBP3 mutations cause hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, lactic acidosis and encephalopathy. || No direct dependency claim; appears only in RBP-based prognostic signatures (e.g. laryngeal cancer). DepMap (this project): median +0.09, 0.3% of models < -0.5.
key_refs: PMID:15509579 - Umeda 2005 JBC, GTPBP3/MTO1 and the mitochondrial wobble modification || PMID:25434004 - GTPBP3 mutations cause a mitochondrial translation defect with cardiomyopathy, lactic acidosis and encephalopathy || PMID:25434004 - Kopajtich 2014 AJHG, GTPBP3 mutations cause a mitochondrial translation defect with cardiomyopathy || PMID:29348686 - Boutoual 2018 Sci Rep, MTO1 and GTPBP3 defects reprogram metabolism via HIF-PPARgamma-UCP2-AMPK || PMID:29390138 - GTPBP3 knockout cells show respiratory defects and reduced mitochondrial translation; patient cells lack tau-m5U34 || PMID:35985767 - GTPBP3 in a prognostic RBP signature for laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
notes: NextGen DepMap: Weakly Selective, only 2/147 dependent lines - markedly weaker than its partner MTO1, which is worth checking (possible GTPase-independent residual activity or guide quality). || I classified it as writer-cofactor because the methyl/taurine transfer chemistry is attributed to MTO1 while GTPBP3 provides GTPase-dependent activation; some authors treat the pair as a single bifunctional enzyme.

complex: tRNA-dependent ATPase that binds Elongator directly (PSTK-like fold)
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer-dependency claim in the literature. DepMap nevertheless scores KTI12 as pan-essential, which is notable for an accessory regulator and may reflect Elongator-independent functions.
key_refs: PMID:30916349 - crystal structure of Kti12; tRNA-dependent ATPase that binds Elongator and whose ATP hydrolysis is required for proper anticodon modification in vivo
notes: Mechanistic link between Elongator and the selenocysteine pathway (PSTK similarity). Human evidence is largely by homology/structure; yeast genetics is the primary source - hence 'established' rather than 'core'. NextGen DepMap: Pan-dependency, 135/147 dependent lines.

complex: two-domain E1-like adenylase + rhodanese (RHD); activates and thiocarboxylates URM1 (and MOCS2A for Moco)
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer-dependency claim; MOCS3 is pan-essential in DepMap. Its dual role (tRNA thiolation and molybdenum-cofactor synthesis) means dependency cannot be attributed to s2U alone.
key_refs: PMID:19145231 - Uba4/MOCS3 adenylates and transfers sulfur onto Urm1 in vitro || PMID:22453920 - MOCS3 is shared between molybdenum-cofactor biosynthesis and tRNA thiolation; adenylates and sulfurates both MOCS2A and URM1
notes: Dual-pathway gene (flag when interpreting). NextGen DepMap: Pan-dependency, 131/147 dependent lines.

complex: NFS1-LYRM4(ISD11)-ACP cysteine desulfurase; persulfide donor for TRMU (and for all Fe-S cluster assembly) | cysteine desulfurase (with LYRM4/ISD11 and NDUFAB1/mtACP for ISC); cytosolic pool transfers sulfur to MOCS3-RHD
cancer_dependency_claims: NFS1 is a genuine context-dependent cancer dependency, but for iron-sulfur-cluster rather than tRNA reasons: above physiological oxygen, cancer cells require high NFS1, NFS1 lies in a region amplified in lung adenocarcinoma and is highest in well-differentiated adenocarcinoma, suppression blocks metastatic and primary lung tumour growth, and insufficient Fe-S maintenance plus glutathione-synthesis inhibition triggers ferroptosis. Pan-essential in DepMap. || NFS1 is a well-known cancer dependency (notably in lung adenocarcinoma/high-oxygen contexts and ferroptosis protection), but that dependency is driven by Fe-S cluster biogenesis, not by tRNA 2-thiolation. DepMap (this project): median -1.49, 99% of models < -0.5 - effectively pan-essential.

notes: HEAVILY CONFOUNDED for an epitranscriptomic analysis: Fe-S cluster biogenesis dominates the phenotype. Included because it is the upstream sulfur source for both cytosolic (URM1/MOCS3/CTU1-2) and mitochondrial (TRMU) 2-thiouridylation. NextGen DepMap: Pan-dependency, 144/147 dependent lines, but 3D organoids LESS sensitive than 2D (-1.454 vs -1.685, FDR<0.001) - an oxygen/metabolism-consistent growth-format effect. || Included for completeness as the obligate sulfur donor, but flagged: its DepMap essentiality is an Fe-S/ferroptosis phenotype and should NOT be interpreted as an RNA-modification dependency. Consider analysing it as a positive control/confounder rather than a pathway member.

complex: ubiquitin-like sulfur-carrier protein; thiocarboxylated by MOCS3 and delivered to CTU1/CTU2
cancer_dependency_claims: No gene-specific cancer-dependency claim; URM1 is pan-essential in DepMap, and reviews note that elevated tRNA-modifying enzyme levels promote some cancers and metastasis. Effects are expected to mirror CTU1/CTU2 and ALKBH8.
key_refs: PMID:19145231 - Urm1 acts as a sulfur carrier in eukaryotic tRNA thiolation, with Uba4 (MOCS3), Ncs2/Ncs6 (CTU2/CTU1) || PMID:33499055 - review of Urm1 as a non-canonical UBL and its mcm5s2U sulfur-carrier role
notes: Also conjugates to proteins (urmylation), so loss is not purely a tRNA phenotype. NextGen DepMap: Pan-dependency, 109/147 dependent lines.

complex: nucleolar
cancer_dependency_claims: SIRT7 has many published cancer roles, but essentially all are via protein deacetylation (notably H3K18ac) rather than RNA ac4C. In the local DepMap NextGen tables SIRT7 is Weakly Selective with 1 NextGen dependent line and a Non-dependency in organoids, so there is no pan-cancer dependency.
key_refs: Nuclear RNA-acetylation can be erased by the deacetylase SIRT7 - bioRxiv 2021 preprint (10.1101/2021.04.06.438707) || Xu et al. 2021 Genome Instability & Disease - SIRT7 reported as an NAD+-independent deacetylase of ac4C on ribosomal RNA (DOI 10.1007/s42764-021-00046-x)
notes: Deliberately tiered as proposed, bordering on controversial: the claim rests on one short communication in a low-visibility journal plus a preprint, with no independent replication that I could find, and most reviews still describe ac4C as having no established eraser. Not PubMed-indexed, so cited without a PMID.

complex: nucleolar; ribosome biogenesis
cancer_dependency_claims: Proposed in 2025 as the ac4C reader that mediates NAT10-induced translation of PPAN and MYC in colorectal cancer. In the local DepMap NextGen tables MYBBP1A is Pan-dependency (110 NextGen; 76 organoid lines) - but as a nucleolar ribosome-biogenesis factor, so pan-essentiality almost certainly does not report on ac4C reading.
key_refs: PMID:41455833 - NAT10 drives CRC via PPAN-regulated DNA damage repair; MYBBP1A identified as a new ac4C reader protein mediating PPAN and MYC translation
notes: Newest addition in this family (Dec 2025) and the first named ac4C reader, so worth having in the catalogue, but single-lab and embedded in a larger cancer-mechanism paper rather than a dedicated binding study. Heavily confounded in DepMap by its nucleolar role.

complex: NAT10-THUMPD1 (tRNA); NAT10 guided by SNORD13 snoRNA (18S helix 45); homodimer
cancer_dependency_claims: The strongest ac4C dependency candidate: NAT10 is the sole eukaryotic ac4C writer, is overexpressed in hepatocellular, colorectal and gastric cancers, is the target of the small molecule Remodelin, and in colorectal cancer drives malignancy and DNA-damage repair through ac4C-dependent translation of PPAN and MYC. In the local DepMap NextGen tables NAT10 is Pan-dependency (137 NextGen; 98 organoid lines), i.e. pan-essential - consistent with its requirement for 18S rRNA processing.
key_refs: PMID:25411247 - human NAT10 is an ATP-dependent RNA acetyltransferase forming ac4C1842 in 18S rRNA; knockdown blocks 18S maturation and retards growth || PMID:30449621 - Arango 2018 Cell: NAT10-dependent ac4C in mRNA enhances stability and translation efficiency || PMID:42321159 - cryo-EM structure of eukaryotic NAT10 and mechanism of THUMPD1-dependent tRNA acetylation; catalytic activity required in cells
notes: rRNA and tRNA ac4C are solid (core). mRNA ac4C is contested: Georgeson & Schwartz (PMID:38640895) reanalysed RedaC:T data and found no reproducible evidence for ac4C within human mRNA, while the original lab and newer low-input methods (PMID:39982985, mouse oocyte ac4C LACE-seq) maintain the mRNA mark. Because NAT10 is pan-essential via ribosome biogenesis, a DepMap hit cannot be used to argue for mRNA ac4C.

complex: NAT10-THUMPD1 (yeast Kre33-Tan1 equivalent)
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer dependency claim; the human phenotype is a syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder from bi-allelic loss of function. In the local DepMap NextGen tables THUMPD1 is Weakly Selective with 6 NextGen and 3 organoid dependent lines - notably much weaker than NAT10, which fits the model that only the tRNA (not the essential rRNA) branch of NAT10 activity requires THUMPD1.
key_refs: PMID:35196516 - bi-allelic THUMPD1 loss-of-function abolishes ac4C in small RNAs and tRNA-Ser-CGA in patients and in CRISPR knockout cell lines || PMID:42321159 - biochemical reconstitution showing THUMPD1 is the adapter enabling NAT10-catalysed tRNA acetylation
notes: Obligate adapter for the tRNA ac4C12 branch only; dispensable for 18S rRNA acetylation, which instead uses the SNORD13 snoRNA guide. The NAT10 vs THUMPD1 dependency gap in DepMap is therefore informative and is a clean internal control for separating rRNA from tRNA ac4C biology.

complex: functions with ASCC complex for DNA repair (not required for RNA demethylation)
cancer_dependency_claims: Highly expressed in prostate, pancreatic and other carcinomas; knockdown impairs proliferation and nascent protein synthesis with accumulation of methylated tRNA (PMID:28205560), and ALKBH3-driven m1A removal makes tRNA angiogenin-cleavable, generating pro-survival tDRs that support xenograft growth (PMID:30541109). Presented as a druggable, lineage-enriched (not pan-essential) dependency.
key_refs: PMID:28205560 - Ueda 2017 Sci Rep: ALKBH3 demethylates endogenous RNA m1A/m3C and supports cancer protein synthesis || PMID:30541109 - Chen 2019 NAR: ALKBH3 is an m1A/m3C tRNA demethylase promoting cancer via tRNA-derived small RNAs || PMID:31815430 - Seo & Kleiner 2019 ACS Chem Biol: ALKBH3 depletion raises m1A and destabilises m1A-containing transcripts
notes: Dual DNA (1-meA/3-meC repair) and RNA demethylase; originally characterised as a DNA repair enzyme, so DepMap signal may reflect either arm.

complex: Standalone mitochondrial Fe(II)/2-OG dioxygenase
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer dependency claim. ALKBH7 loss reduces mitochondria-encoded tRNA levels, mitochondrial translation and respiration (PMID:34253897), so any dependency would be metabolic/OXPHOS-linked. Generally non-essential. || Only pan-cancer bioinformatic prognostic/immunotherapy analyses (HNSCC, breast cancer, prostate variant) - no dependency evidence. DepMap (this project): median +0.11, 0.3% of models < -0.5.
key_refs: PMID:34253897 - Zhang 2021 Nat Cell Biol, ALKBH7 demethylates m2,2G and m1A within mt-Ile and mt-Leu1 pre-tRNA regions of nascent polycistronic mitochondrial RNA || PMID:34253897 - Zhang 2021 Nat Cell Biol: ALKBH7 demethylates m22G and m1A in nascent polycistronic mitochondrial RNA and controls its processing || PMID:37925186 - Zhang 2023 Methods Enzymol, DAMM-seq method underpinning the ALKBH7 substrate assignment
notes: Single-lab assignment so far (He lab); earlier literature described ALKBH7 as a regulator of programmed necrosis with no nucleic-acid demethylase activity detected, hence 'proposed'. || The only proposed eraser acting on mitochondrial tRNA-region methylation; its function is on nascent polycistronic pre-tRNA junctions and regulates processing rather than mature-tRNA marks. Single-group evidence to date, hence 'proposed'. Alkbh7 knockout mice have metabolic/obesity phenotypes.

complex: eNoSC (with SIRT1 and SUV39H1) for rDNA silencing; acts alone for 28S m1A1322
cancer_dependency_claims: RRP8/NML depletion impairs 60S subunit formation, frees RPL11, stabilises p53 via RPL11-MDM2 and arrests growth p53-dependently (PMID:27149924) - i.e. the dependency is predicted to be stronger in TP53-wild-type lines, a testable DepMap interaction. No direct oncogene-addiction claim.
key_refs: PMID:27149924 - Waku 2016 J Cell Sci: NML/RRP8 required for 28S m1A; loss triggers RPL11-MDM2-p53 || PMID:30093689 - Sharma 2018 Sci Rep: NML is the human 28S m1A1322 methyltransferase (helix 25.1)
notes: Human homolog of yeast Rrp8. Also has a chromatin/energy-sensing role in eNoSC, so phenotypes are not purely rRNA-methylation driven.

cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer dependency claim; modifies a single nuclear-encoded tRNA (tRNA-Asp), so a strong dependency would be surprising. Useful as a specificity control.

notes: The only known cytosolic m1A9 writer in humans - belongs in the m1A bucket despite the TRMT10 (m1G) family name.

No lineage-selective oncogenic dependency claim specific to its methyltransferase activity. || Mostly expression/prognosis: TRMT10C predicts poorer survival and supports malignant behaviour in gynaecological cancers; a lncRNA-derived micropeptide (MRPIP) attenuates HCC by disrupting HSD17B10 tetramerization and HSD17B10-TRMT10C subcomplex formation, implying tumours depend on an intact subcomplex (Zhu 2025 Mol Cell); a 2024 paper claims TRMT10C-mediated m7G of circFAM126A in lung cancer.
