The m7G-on-circRNA claim is mechanistically implausible for a Trm10-family enzyme and should be treated as unverified.

complex: TRMT6-TRMT61A (alpha2beta2 heterotetramer; TRMT61A = catalytic subunit)
cancer_dependency_claims: TRMT6/TRMT61A are overexpressed in advanced HCC and correlate with poor survival; the complex is required for liver tumourigenesis via m1A-dependent PPARdelta translation -> cholesterol synthesis -> Hedgehog activation in liver CSCs, and a small-molecule TRMT6/61A inhibitor had anti-tumour effect (PMID:34728628). Overexpressed in urothelial bladder carcinoma, where m1A on tRF-3s rewires the tRF targetome and the UPR (PMID:35444240). Not pan-essential in DepMap-type screens; dependency appears context/lineage-selective.

notes: Canonical tRNA m1A58 methyltransferase. Its mRNA substrates are restricted to tRNA-T-loop-like structures and are low-stoichiometry; the once-claimed widespread 5'UTR m1A was shown to be antibody cap cross-reactivity (PMID:31719534), so treat 'mRNA m1A writer' as a real but narrow activity.

complex: Standalone (does not require TRMT6, unlike nuclear TRMT61A-TRMT6) | homo-oligomer (homotetramer-like, bacterial-type; does NOT need TRMT6)
cancer_dependency_claims: No strong cancer-specific dependency claim published. Germline TRMT61B variants are associated with Wilms tumour, hepatoblastoma and neuroblastoma risk in Chinese cohorts. DepMap (this project): median +0.02, 1.7% of models < -0.5 - no broad dependency, so the aneuploidy-selective claim needs explicit aneuploidy-score interaction testing.

The aneuploidy association is the most DepMap-testable hypothesis here (CN/aneuploidy covariates are available).

complex: mt-RNase P methyltransferase subcomplex with TRMT10C (also a short-chain dehydrogenase, isoleucine/steroid metabolism) | mtRNase P; obligate tetrameric partner of TRMT10C (MRPP1-MRPP2 subcomplex)

Mutations cause HSD10 mitochondrial disease, which argues the moonlighting RNA function is dose-sensitive in normal tissue too. || Pan-cancer multi-omics profiling proposes prognostic and metabolic/immune roles; overexpression increased pheochromocytoma cell growth and death resistance; targeted indirectly in HCC via the MRPIP micropeptide that blocks its tetramerization (Zhu 2025 Mol Cell). Also recovered in genome-wide CRISPR screens of mitochondrial-dysfunction sensing. DepMap (this project): median -0.34, 36% of models < -0.5, CEGv2 gene.

Include, but interpret DepMap signal cautiously (two unrelated functions). || Moonlighting: a bona fide SDR dehydrogenase (isoleucine/2-methyl-3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA) AND an obligate RNA-modification cofactor; HSD10 disease phenotypes track the RNA function more than the dehydrogenase. Separately, TRMT2A is irreversibly crosslinked to tRNA by 5-fluorouracil, suggesting an RNA-dependent route of 5-FU cytotoxicity (PMID:31361898) - an attractive drug-response hypothesis to test against 5-FU sensitivity data. || TRMT2A behaves mainly as a biomarker/suppressor: TRMT2A protein expression independently predicts recurrence in HER2-positive breast cancer across three institutional cohorts, and TRMT2A over-expression suppresses proliferation while its loss increases growth, making it a candidate cell-cycle regulator. It is also proposed as a 5-fluorouracil target, because 5-FU-substituted tRNA traps TRMT2A, offering an alternative mechanism of 5-FU cytotoxicity. DepMap: non-dependency.

The 5-FU-crosslinking result makes TRMT2A the best candidate in this family for a drug-sensitivity (rather than viability) analysis. || m5U54 loss promotes angiogenin-dependent tRNA cleavage and 5'tiRNA formation (PMID:33799331) - a stress-response link. 5-FU mechanism: PMID:32348733. cancer_dependency_claims: Context-dependent oncogene (MLL-rearranged leukaemia) or tumour suppressor (several solid tumours), in both cases via DNA 5hmC rather than RNA. In the local DepMap NextGen tables TET1 is Weakly Selective with 1 dependent line in each panel.

cancer_dependency_claims: TET2 is a bona fide tumour suppressor in myeloid malignancies, but through DNA 5mC oxidation - loss-of-function, not dependency. cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer dependency claims attributable to RNA activity. In the local DepMap NextGen tables TET3 is a Non-dependency with 0 dependent lines in both panels.

complex: TREX mRNA export complex (THOC subunits, UAP56/DDX39B, NXF1)

cancer_dependency_claims: LIN28B is an independent oncogene (notably in MYCN-driven neuroblastoma) and was proposed as a novel m5C mediator that stabilises NSUN2-methylated GRB2 mRNA to activate PI3K/AKT and ERK/MAPK in oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma. complex: SR protein splicing machinery
cancer_dependency_claims: Directly links the epitranscriptome to a recurrent cancer driver mutation: the MDS/AML hotspot SRSF2-P95H impairs m5C binding and reduces occupancy on key leukaemia transcripts, and low NSUN2 plus mutant SRSF2 predicts poor outcome in leukaemia patients. cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer dependency claims. In the local DepMap NextGen tables YBX2 is a Non-dependency with 0 dependent lines in both panels; expression is largely germ-cell restricted, so it is unlikely to produce a signal in a cancer-line screen.

complex: pre-90S / SSU processome; non-catalytic complexes with box C/D snoRNPs (U3, U8)

In the local DepMap NextGen tables NOP2 is classified Pan-dependency (143 NextGen dependent lines; 104 organoid lines), i.e. pan-essential. Note the discordance: in the local DepMap NextGen tables NSUN2 is a Non-dependency with 0 dependent lines in both NextGen and organoid panels, so published claims are about tumour initiation/stress resistance rather than cell-autonomous proliferation. || Extensive cancer literature (Myc target; required for skin tumour initiation and for stress-induced tRNA fragment biology; many m5C-mRNA oncogenic claims), but essentially none of it tests the mitochondrial pool. Overlap intended.

complex: Standalone SUN-domain m5C methyltransferase; acts with ALKBH1 (m5C34 -> hm5C -> f5C34) on mt-tRNA-Met | none; acts upstream of ALKBH1 in the f5C34 pathway

complex: nucleolar; functional orthologue of yeast Rcm1p
cancer_dependency_claims: Epigenetic silencing of NSUN5 by promoter hypermethylation has been reported in gliomas and linked to altered ribosome function and better response to alkylating chemotherapy (Janin 2019 Acta Neuropathol), i.e. loss is favourable rather than a dependency. Consistent with that, in the local DepMap NextGen tables NSUN5 is Weakly Selective with 1 dependent line in each panel.

complex: none obligate

However in the local DepMap NextGen tables NSUN6 is one of the few Strongly Selective classifications in this family (3 NextGen dependent lines; Weakly Selective with 3 lines in organoids) - a genuinely interesting selective-effect candidate worth following up.

Local DepMap: NextGen class "Strongly Selective" (only 4 dependent lines) and 2D Chronos mean -0.10 - the published selectivity is not reproduced as a strong CRISPR dependency in standard 2D lines.

complex: AlkB-family Fe(II)/2-OG dioxygenase; monomeric | None obligate (Fe(II)/2-OG AlkB-family dioxygenase)

Local DepMap: "Weakly Selective" (3 dependent lines), 2D Chronos mean -0.01 - no detectable pan or broad selective dependency, i.e. published FTO phenotypes do not translate into CRISPR fitness effects in cell lines. || Extensively claimed as an AML/glioblastoma/melanoma dependency and an immunotherapy-resistance factor, but essentially all of that work attributes the effect to m6A or m6Am, not m1A. Another curator will own FTO for m6A/m6Am - expect overlap. || [review] Substrate targeting partly directed by ZBTB48/TZAP (2024); ZBTB48 not included (modulator).

complex: ABC-F family translation factor; acts with eIF2/ribosome in eIF4F-independent initiation
cancer_dependency_claims: No clear m6A-linked cancer-dependency claims; studied mainly in innate immunity and translation. Local DepMap: Hart CEGv2 core essential, NextGen "Pan-dependency" (129/147), 2D Chronos mean -0.74 (90% of lines < -0.5) - strong essentiality driven by its translation-factor role.
key_refs: PMID:29107534 - Coots 2017 Mol Cell: m6A facilitates eIF4F-independent translation with ABCF1 as the critical mediator
notes: Mediator of m6A-promoted cap-independent translation rather than a structurally defined methyl-binding protein; its pan-essentiality is not m6A-specific.

complex: eIF3; direct physical partner of METTL3 in mRNA-looping-dependent translation
cancer_dependency_claims: METTL3-eIF3h interaction is required for enhanced translation of oncogenic mRNAs, densely packed polyribosomes and oncogenic transformation in lung cancer models, where METTL3 loss sensitises cells to BRD4 inhibition. Local DepMap: NextGen "Pan-dependency" (105/147), common-essential flag, 2D Chronos mean -0.64 (70% of lines < -0.5).

notes: Listed as "other" rather than reader/cofactor: it is a writer-interacting effector whose binding is not shown to depend on the mark itself. Included because the family scope explicitly asks about eIF3 subunits.

complex: Centromeric nucleosome / CCAN; reads m6A on centromeric RNA (cenRNA)
cancer_dependency_claims: Cell 2024: cenRNA m6A is elevated in cancerous versus non-cancerous cells, and m6A-modified cenRNA stabilises CENPA to preserve centromere integrity during mitosis - i.e. a cancer-associated m6A axis. DepMap NextGen (local table): Pan-dependency, 139/147 NextGen and 100/108 organoid dependent lines, which is entirely expected from centromere function; any hit would be centromere-driven, not m6A-driven.
key_refs: PMID:39305902 - Cell 2024: m6A-modified cenRNA stabilizes CENPA to ensure centromere integrity in cancer cells; CENPA identified as the m6A reader of cenRNA
notes: Unusual entry (a histone variant as an RNA-modification reader) and heavily confounded in DepMap, but it is a primary Cell paper with explicit reader assignment, and it is the only candidate that extends the catalog to centromeric RNA as a substrate class. Keep tier 'proposed' and expect it to behave as a pan-essential confounder.

complex: eIF3 (13-subunit translation initiation complex)
cancer_dependency_claims: eIF3 subunits are broadly essential and eIF3a overexpression is prognostic in several carcinomas, but not as an m6A dependency. Local DepMap: Hart CEGv2 core essential, NextGen "Pan-dependency" (144/147), 2D Chronos mean -1.28 (84% of lines < -1).

notes: The m6A-binding activity was mapped to the eIF3 complex (eIF3a used as the representative subunit), not to a dedicated reader domain; other eIF3 subunits are excluded to avoid importing the whole complex. Any CRISPR signal is core translation essentiality.

complex: ELAV/Hu family; functionally opposed to m6A-mediated decay
cancer_dependency_claims: HuR is a long-standing oncogenic RNA-stability factor (COX2, VEGF, MYC) across colorectal, pancreatic and breast cancer with inhibitor programmes, but its m6A link is indirect. Local DepMap: NextGen "Strongly Selective" (27 dependent lines), 2D Chronos mean -0.18.
key_refs: PMID:24394384 - Wang 2014 Nat Cell Biol: m6A methylation decreases HuR binding and destabilises developmental regulators
notes: Controversial/indirect: m6A reduces rather than creates HuR binding (anti-correlated, like an m6A-repelled factor), and most HuR cancer biology is independent of m6A. Kept in the catalog because the family scope lists it, but it should be down-weighted in any RWE enrichment test.

complex: FMRP-FXR1/FXR2 family; reported to compete with/hand off to YTHDF2

In the local DepMap NextGen tables FMR1 is a Non-dependency with 0 dependent lines in both panels. || Essentially no cancer-dependency literature in the m6A context (FMR1 is the fragile-X gene); scattered reports of FMRP supporting tumour-cell invasion. Local DepMap: NextGen "Non-dependency" (0 dependent lines), 2D Chronos mean +0.07.

notes: Listed because it is in scope. Evidence that FMRP binding is methylation-dependent is limited and largely secondary/review-level; FMRP is a promiscuous mRNA-binding protein, so apparent m5C enrichment may be indirect. Keep as a low-confidence reader. || Mark-dependent binding shown in two orthogonal proteomics approaches, but function is context-dependent; paralogues FXR1/FXR2 lack comparable evidence and are excluded.

complex: None defined for the methyl-reading function
cancer_dependency_claims: FUS is a well-known fusion oncogene partner (FUS-DDIT3 in myxoid liposarcoma, FUS-ERG in leukaemia), but none of that is m6A/m1A-dependent, so it is not an epitranscriptomic dependency claim. complex: Stress-granule core (G3BP1/G3BP2, CAPRIN1, USP10)
cancer_dependency_claims: G3BP1 is implicated in stress-granule-dependent survival, Ras signalling and metastasis in several cancers, but not as an m6A-pathway dependency. complex: Stress-granule core; G3BP1 paralogue
cancer_dependency_claims: Reported in prostate and breast cancer progression via stress-granule/NF-kB routes; no m6A-specific dependency claims. Local DepMap: "Weakly Selective" (1 dependent line), 2D Chronos mean -0.05.

notes: Included with G3BP1 as the m6A-repelled pair named in the family scope; evidence is from the same two proteomics studies, so treat as one line of evidence.

complex: hnRNP C1/C2 tetramer; U-tract binder

complex: IGF2BP1/2/3 family; with ELAVL1/HuR, MATR3, PABPC1 in stabilising mRNP

complex: IGF2BP family

complex: Cleavage/polyadenylation factor CFIIm (PCF11-CLP1); binds RNA Pol II CTD

So the published claim is a differentiation/therapy-response modifier, not a viability dependency. DepMap NextGen (local tda_dependency_classification table): Pan-dependency, 100/147 NextGen dependent lines; High Variance with 62/108 in organoids - a strong but 3'-end-processing-driven signal, the same confounder class as the excluded SRSF3/NXF1.

notes: BIGGEST SINGLE GAP I FOUND: the union contains m6Am writers (PCIF1, METTL4) and an eraser (FTO) but NO m6Am reader, and the field's stated obstacle ('m6Am function remains controversial because the m6Am reader is unknown') was resolved in 2024. PCF11 is a genuine mark-dependent binder (m6Am-dependent sequestration away from Pol II), so it passes the reader test, but it is also a core 3'-end processing factor and pan-dependent, so treat it like SRSF3: include for completeness, interpret with care. Single lab so far - tier 'proposed'.

complex: PRRC2 family (PRRC2A/B/C); stabilises targets in competition with YTHDF2
cancer_dependency_claims: Few direct cancer-dependency claims (scattered reports in glioma and gastric cancer); originally characterised in oligodendrocyte development. notes: Single-lab reader assignment (GGACU binding via a non-YTH region, stabilising Olig2 mRNA); paralogues PRRC2B/C have no m6A evidence and are excluded. The CNS/brain lineage arm of the NextGen dataset is the natural place to test it.

complex: Recruits RBM15 and thereby the METTL3/METTL14 MTC to chromatin-associated RNA

This is a differentiation-block (AML) claim rather than a proliferation dependency, and DepMap matches that: Weakly Selective, 1/147 NextGen dependent lines and Non-dependency in organoids, so expect no CRISPR viability signal.

notes: A Nature-family primary paper with explicit mark-dependent binding (caRNA m6A), which puts it well above several entries the union already carries as 'proposed' (ABCF1, RBM45, EIF3A). Note the dual nature: reader AND writer-targeting factor - I classified it as reader because the binding is mark-dependent, but the RBM15 recruitment makes it a writer-targeting factor too.

complex: RBM33-ALKBH5 complex (recruits and activates the eraser by promoting ALKBH5 deSUMOylation)

complex: Homo-oligomeric (HOA domain) RRM protein
cancer_dependency_claims: No meaningful cancer-dependency literature (studied in neurodevelopment and ALS/FTD inclusions). Local DepMap: "Weakly Selective" (10 dependent lines), 2D Chronos mean -0.05.

notes: Mark preference is modest and partly m6A-independent in function; individual RRMs do not prefer m6A (full-length synergy proposed). Proposed tier.

complex: hnRNP G; low-complexity RGG region mediates m6A-switch binding

notes: Same m6A-switch mechanism as HNRNPC (structure-mediated, RGG-dependent). Include for scope completeness but treat its strong CRISPR effect as core RNA-processing essentiality, and note RBMXL1/RBMX2 paralogues are also pan-essential.

complex: RISC-associated; four staphylococcal-nuclease-like domains plus a Tudor domain. In cancer biology it is best known as the binding partner and effector of MTDH/AEG-1 (MTDH-SND1 axis). | Tudor-SN; part of RISC-associated/Tudor staphylococcal nuclease module

Crucially, none of these claims depend on inosine recognition, so any DepMap dependency for SND1 should not be read as evidence for an epitranscriptomic mechanism. || SND1 is widely described as an oncogene in hepatocellular carcinoma, breast and prostate cancer (lipid metabolism, NF-kB, RNA stability), though usually independently of m6A. Local DepMap: NextGen "Non-dependency" (0 dependent lines), 2D Chronos mean +0.05 - no dependency.
key_refs: PMID:15895094 - Scadden 2005 Nat Struct Mol Biol: Tudor-SN specifically binds and promotes cleavage of hyper-edited dsRNA containing multiple I:U / U:I pairs || PMID:31647415 - Baquero-Perez 2019 eLife: the Tudor protein SND1 is an m6A reader essential for KSHV replication

It is the main candidate 'inosine reader' in the literature besides ENDOV, so it belongs in the catalog, but flag it as a likely confound: a positive DepMap hit for SND1 is far more plausibly MTDH-axis biology than mark reading. || Reader claim comes from a virology context (m6A-dependent binding to ORF50 RNA); mammalian-cell generality is unproven, hence proposed.

complex: None for the m6A function; functions with the m6A machinery (YTHDF2 identified as the strongest genetic modifier)
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer-dependency claim; the biology is ALS/FTD (TDP-43 proteinopathy), with RNA hypermethylation in ALS spinal cord and YTHDF2 knockdown prolonging survival of ALS patient neurons. DepMap NextGen (local table): Pan-dependency, 143/147 NextGen and 105/108 organoid dependent lines - a pan-essential splicing/RNA-metabolism gene, so any dependency hit is uninterpretable as m6A biology. Add for catalog completeness and as a known confounder, not as a candidate target.
key_refs: PMID:36634675 - McMillan 2023 Mol Cell: TDP43 recognizes m6A RNA; RNA methylation is critical for TDP43 binding and autoregulation; m6A factors modify TDP43 toxicity in primary neurons
notes: Strong primary evidence of mark-dependence (binding lost on unmethylated substrate) in a top journal, which is why I propose it even though it is pan-essential. Flag it in the analysis alongside the other pan-essential readers so the set-level tests are not driven by it.

complex: Nuclear YTH reader; partners SRSF3/SRSF10 (splicing), NXF1 (export), forms m6A-dependent nuclear YTHDC1 bodies (YDCs) | nuclear; m6A-dependent SRSF3/NXF1 recruitment
cancer_dependency_claims: YTHDC1 is required for AML/leukaemogenesis - it sustains MCM-complex-mediated DNA replication and forms phase-separated nuclear bodies that suppress myeloid differentiation; it is also implicated in endometrial and lung cancer. Local DepMap: the strongest reader dependency - NextGen "Pan-dependency" (105/147 lines, organoid mean -0.91) though not flagged common-essential; 2D Chronos mean -0.36 (15% of lines < -0.5). || Reported as an AML dependency and an XIST/m6A effector, again as an m6A reader. No cancer dependency claim based on m1A binding.
key_refs: PMID:26876937 - Xiao 2016 Mol Cell: nuclear m6A reader YTHDC1 regulates mRNA splicing || PMID:28984244 - Roundtree 2017 eLife: YTHDC1 mediates nuclear export of m6A mRNA || PMID:29791134 - Dai 2018 Anal Chem: YTHDC1 binds m1A-containing RNA in vitro (YTHDC2 does not) || PMID:34255814 - Sheng 2021 Blood: YTHDC1 is critical in leukaemogenesis via MCM-mediated DNA replication
notes: Note the large gap between organoid/NextGen (-0.91) and standard 2D (-0.36) effects - a candidate for the 3D-vs-2D differential-dependency analysis in this dataset. || Weakest-supported m1A reader of the set: single study, in vitro binding only.

complex: YTHDC2-MEIOC (obligate germline partner); ANKRD domain binds XRN1; 3'-5' RNA helicase
cancer_dependency_claims: Mainly a meiosis/germline factor; cancer claims are sparse (colon cancer HIF-1alpha, testicular/germ-cell tumours). Local DepMap: "Weakly Selective" (1 dependent line), 2D Chronos mean -0.02 - no dependency.
