notes: Keep the caveat: YTHDC2 is a bona fide YTH-domain m6A binder biochemically (weak affinity), but two 2022 studies showed its in vivo germline function needs the helicase/XRN1 axis and not m6A recognition - so its mark-dependence is disputed even though its reader identity is not.

complex: YTHDF paralogue family (YTHDF1/2/3); interacts with eIF3 / translation machinery
cancer_dependency_claims: YTHDF1 is best known as a host target for immunotherapy: Ythdf1 loss in dendritic cells enhances cross-presentation and anti-PD-L1 efficacy; it is also reported to promote gastric, colorectal, lung and ovarian cancer growth. Local DepMap: NextGen class "Non-dependency" (0 dependent lines), 2D Chronos mean +0.03 - no cell-autonomous dependency. || Well-known m6A-reader dependency claims (e.g. colorectal/gastric cancer, anti-tumour immunity), but no cancer phenotype has been causally attributed to m1A binding. Rarely essential in CRISPR screens.
key_refs: PMID:26046440 - Wang 2015 Cell: YTHDF1 promotes translation of m6A-modified mRNA || PMID:29791134 - Dai 2018 Anal Chem: quantitative proteomics identifies YTHDF1-3 and YTHDC1 as direct m1A binders in vitro || PMID:30728504 - Han 2019 Nature: anti-tumour immunity controlled via m6A and YTHDF1 in dendritic cells || PMID:32492408 - Zaccara 2020 Cell: unified model - YTHDF1/2/3 act redundantly to destabilise m6A mRNAs
notes: The Zaccara/Jaffrey unified model argues YTHDF1/2/3 are functionally redundant (all promoting decay) rather than division-of-labour readers; the triple-paralogue redundancy predicts weak single-gene CRISPR effects, which is exactly what the data show. || The m1A-reader assignment rests on in vitro binding plus transcriptome co-localisation. Given that high-stoichiometry mRNA m1A is now known to be very rare (PMID:31719534), physiological m1A reading by YTHDF1 is doubtful - flagged controversial.

complex: YTHDF family; recruits CCR4-NOT (via CNOT1) and RNase P/MRP-RIDA for decay | recruits CCR4-NOT (CNOT1) for decay
cancer_dependency_claims: YTHDF2 is a selective dependency of AML leukaemia stem cells (sparing normal HSCs) and of glioblastoma stem cells (maintaining MYC/oncogene expression), and is the most commonly nominated druggable m6A reader. Local DepMap: NextGen "High Variance" (18 dependent lines), 2D Chronos mean -0.25 with 11% of lines < -0.5 - a modest, selective dependency consistent with the stem-cell-restricted claims. || Strong published dependencies in AML leukaemia stem cells and in glioblastoma stem cells, and a role in NK-cell anti-tumour immunity - all framed as m6A-reader functions. The m1A-reader work shows m1A-dependent, methylation-specific binding and that YTHDF2 depletion stabilises m1A-containing transcripts (PMID:31815430), but no cancer phenotype has been pinned to m1A.
key_refs: PMID:24284625 - Wang 2013 Nature: YTHDF2 mediates m6A-dependent mRNA decay || PMID:29791134 - Dai 2018 Anal Chem: W432 in the YTH aromatic cage is needed for m1A recognition || PMID:31031138 - Paris 2019 Cell Stem Cell: YTHDF2 as an AML cancer-stem-cell dependency || PMID:31815430 - Seo & Kleiner 2019 ACS Chem Biol: YTHDF2 recognises m1A-modified RNA and is associated with transcript destabilisation || PMID:33023892 - Dixit 2020 Cancer Discov: YTHDF2 is a targetable dependency in glioblastoma stem cells
notes: Strongest prior for a selective reader dependency. Because the published claims are stem-cell/3D specific, the NextGen 3D-organoid and GBM-state comparisons in this dataset are the right place to test it rather than bulk 2D means. || Best-supported of the four putative m1A readers (two independent labs, mutational evidence), but still controversial as a bona fide in vivo m1A reader.

complex: YTHDF family; cooperates with YTHDF1/2
cancer_dependency_claims: YTHDF3 induces translation of m6A-enriched transcripts (ST6GALNAC5, GJA1, EGFR) to promote breast-cancer brain metastasis, and is implicated in prostate, ovarian and liver cancer. Local DepMap caveat: in the post-26Q1 2D Chronos matrix only 74 of 1208 models have a YTHDF3 score (mean -0.09); NextGen class is "Weakly Selective" (1 dependent line) - so sparse guide/gene coverage, not biology, dominates any YTHDF3 readout here. || Many m6A-based claims (e.g. breast cancer brain metastasis). For m1A specifically, YTHDF3 was reported to bind m1A-methylated IGF1R mRNA and promote its decay in trophoblasts (PMID:32194978) - a non-cancer model; no cancer dependency attributed to m1A reading.
key_refs: PMID:28106072 - Shi 2017 Cell Res: YTHDF3 facilitates translation and decay of m6A RNA || PMID:28106076 - Li 2017 Cell Res: cytoplasmic YTHDF3 promotes translation || PMID:29791134 - Dai 2018 Anal Chem: YTHDF3 binds m1A in vitro || PMID:32194978 - Zheng 2020 Cell Discov: cytoplasmic m1A reader YTHDF3 destabilises m1A-methylated IGF1R || PMID:33125861 - Chang 2020 Cancer Cell: YTHDF3 drives breast-cancer brain metastasis
notes: Practical flag for the user: check per-gene n before interpreting - YTHDF3 is the one m6A RWE gene in this matrix with badly incomplete coverage (74/1208 models). || Controversial for the same reason as YTHDF1/2; the trophoblast paper relies on m1A antibody-based mapping, which is the exact methodology later shown to be cap-cross-reactive.

complex: YTHDC2-MEIOC heterodimer
cancer_dependency_claims: No meaningful cancer-dependency literature (meiosis-restricted). Local DepMap: "Weakly Selective" (11 dependent lines), 2D Chronos mean -0.21.
key_refs: Abby 2016 Nat Commun - MEIOC as a meiosis-specific YTHDC2 partner || PMID:29033321 - Wojtas 2017 Mol Cell: YTHDC2 acts in a complex with MEIOC in the meiotic programme || Soh 2017 PLoS Genetics - Meioc is required with Ythdc2 for the meiotic programme
notes: Included as the only well-documented obligate partner of a YTH reader: MEIOC stabilises YTHDC2 and is required for its germline function. Expect no cancer signal; useful as a scope-completeness entry rather than a candidate.

complex: Acts largely as a monomer (VCR/MTase + vertebrate-conserved regions); no obligate partner known
cancer_dependency_claims: METTL16 drives AML/leukaemia stem-cell self-renewal by reprogramming BCAA metabolism (BCAT1/2) and promotes HCC, colorectal, gastric and ccRCC growth; it also has an m6A-independent cytoplasmic function promoting translation initiation via eIF3a/eIF3b. Local DepMap: strong pan-essential - member of Hart CEGv2, NextGen "Pan-dependency" (140/147 lines), 2D Chronos mean -0.92 (91% < -0.5, 39% < -1), 3D organoid mean -1.39.
key_refs: PMID:28525753 - Pendleton 2017 Cell: METTL16 methylates U6 snRNA A43 and the MAT2A hairpins controlling SAM homeostasis || PMID:35145225 - Su 2022 Nat Cell Biol: m6A-independent METTL16 function in translation and HCC tumorigenesis || PMID:36608679 - Han 2023 Cell Stem Cell: METTL16 drives leukaemogenesis via BCAA metabolism
notes: Dual mark/target set: U6 snRNA m6A43 plus structured mRNA hairpins (MAT2A, MALAT1). Its near-universal essentiality is probably dominated by SAM homeostasis (MAT2A) and the m6A-independent translation role rather than by mRNA m6A - important caveat before calling it an "m6A dependency".

complex: m6A-METTL complex (MACOM+MAC); catalytic subunit of the MAC heterodimer METTL3-METTL14, nucleated on WTAP/VIRMA/ZC3H13/CBLL1/RBM15(B)
cancer_dependency_claims: METTL3 is required for AML maintenance (SAM-competitive inhibitor STM2457 reduces leukaemia burden in vivo) and has been called a dependency in AML, lung, bladder, glioma and many other tumours; it also promotes translation of oncogenic mRNAs (e.g. BRD4, SP1/SP2). In the local DepMap data it is a broad but sub-maximal dependency: NextGen (Nature 2026) class "Pan-dependency" and flagged common-essential, post-26Q1 2D Chronos rescaled mean -0.54 (58% of 1208 lines < -0.5, only 1% < -1), i.e. consistently but modestly depleted rather than a hard core essential.
key_refs: PMID:24316715 - Liu 2013 Nat Chem Biol: METTL3-METTL14 complex is the nuclear m6A writer || PMID:29186125 - Barbieri 2017 Nature: promoter-bound METTL3 maintains AML by m6A-dependent translation || PMID:33902106 - Yankova 2021 Nature: STM2457 METTL3 inhibition as AML therapy
notes: Only catalytic m6A writer for the bulk of internal mRNA m6A; MTase (MT-A70) domain is the drug target. Note that part of its reported phenotypes (promoter/chromatin, translation-enhancing METTL3-eIF3h looping) may be partly m6A-independent, which matters when interpreting CRISPR scores.

complex: MT-A70 family; no obligate partner established
cancer_dependency_claims: Few credible cancer-dependency claims; scattered reports in breast/lung cancer and hypoxia signalling. Local DepMap: "Weakly Selective" (1 dependent line), 2D Chronos mean +0.06 and organoid mean +0.05 - no dependency at all.
key_refs: PMID:31913360 - Chen 2020 Cell Res: METTL4 is an snRNA m6Am MTase regulating splicing || PMID:32183942 - Hao 2020 Mol Cell: METTL4 proposed as mitochondrial DNA 6mA methyltransferase || PMID:32813009 - Goh 2020 Nucleic Acids Res: METTL4 catalyses U2 snRNA m6Am (Am30) to regulate pre-mRNA splicing
notes: Marked controversial because the substrate assignment is disputed: internal m6Am of U2 snRNA (A30, on a 2'-O-methylated A) versus mitochondrial DNA N6-methyldeoxyadenosine. Both claims rest on few labs; the DNA-6mA claim is widely questioned on abundance grounds.

complex: METTL5-TRMT112 obligate heterodimer
cancer_dependency_claims: METTL5-deposited 18S m6A1832 promotes translation initiation and breast-cancer cell growth; loss impairs pluripotency/differentiation programmes and (in humans) causes microcephaly/intellectual disability. Local DepMap: only "Weakly Selective" (3 dependent lines), 2D Chronos mean -0.11 - i.e. essentially dispensable across cell lines despite a core rRNA mark.
key_refs: PMID:31328227 - van Tran 2019 Nucleic Acids Res: METTL5 is the 18S rRNA m6A1832 MTase, stabilised by TRMT112 || PMID:32217665 - Ignatova 2020 Genes Dev: METTL5 in pluripotency and development || PMID:33357433 - Rong 2020 Cell Rep: METTL5 promotes translation initiation and breast cancer growth
notes: A clean example of a core, structurally defined writer with almost no CRISPR dependency - good contrast case against TRMT112 (its own partner), which is pan-essential for unrelated reasons.

complex: Binds the phosphorylated CTD of RNA Pol II; MT-A70 family, functions as monomer | Pol II CTD (Ser5-P)-associated; acts only on cap1 (2'-O-methylated) first adenosine
cancer_dependency_claims: Many single-lab cancer claims (hepatocellular, colorectal, gastric, bladder, head-and-neck), generally oncogenic, plus an immuno-oncology angle in which PCIF1 loss increases interferon/antigen-presentation signalling and sensitises tumours to immunotherapy. Importantly PCIF1 knockout cells and mice are viable, so it is NOT expected to be pan-essential - selectivity in the new DepMap would be genuinely interesting. || PCIF1 has been reported to promote oesophageal squamous-cell carcinoma, renal-cell carcinoma, glioma and multiple myeloma, and - most relevant therapeutically - PCIF1 loss in immune cells enhances antitumour immunity (CD8 T-cell activation/ferroptosis control; blocking PCIF1 releases STAT1-driven Th1 immunity to potentiate immunotherapy). Local DepMap: "Weakly Selective" (12 dependent lines), 2D Chronos mean -0.11 - near-dispensable intrinsically, consistent with an immune/extrinsic rather than cell-autonomous target.
key_refs: PMID:30467178 - Akichika 2018 Science: PCIF1/CAPAM is the cap-specific adenosine N6-methyltransferase || PMID:30467178 - cap-specific terminal N6-methylation of RNA by an RNA polymerase II-associated methyltransferase (Science 2019) || PMID:31279658 - Boulias 2019 Mol Cell: PCIF1 defines the m6Am transcriptome || PMID:31279659 - Sendinc 2019 Mol Cell: PCIF1 catalyses m6Am and regulates gene expression || PMID:32814042 - the mammalian cap-specific m6Am RNA methyltransferase PCIF1 regulates transcript levels in mouse tissues (Cell Rep 2020) || PMID:33982754 - PCIF1/CAPAM is dynamically recruited to promoters in a transcription-dependent manner (J Biochem 2021)
notes: Strictly dependent on prior CMTR1 cap1 Nm, so a CMTR1-PCIF1 epistasis is built into the pathway. The functional consequence of cap m6Am (translation up, down, or neutral) is still disputed across the 2019-2021 papers; the enzyme assignment itself is not. || Only known writer of cap-adjacent m6Am (on 2'-O-methylated first transcribed A); strictly requires the m7G cap and cap1 2'-O-methylation. Its cell-intrinsic dispensability plus immune phenotype is the key framing for any DepMap-based readout. || [review] Proposed PCIF1 cofactor SERBP1 (Nat Commun 2025) and m6Am reader PCF11 (Mol Cell 2024) added to the catalog as proposed.

complex: Monomeric MT-A70-family enzyme (CCHC zinc fingers + GRF); nucleolar
cancer_dependency_claims: ZCCHC4 promotes HCC growth/metastasis, chemoresistance (interfering with DNA-damage-induced apoptosis via lncRNA AL133467.2), and progression of colorectal, glioma, oesophageal and osteosarcoma models; frequently proposed as a prognostic marker. Local DepMap: NextGen class "Non-dependency" (0 dependent lines), 2D Chronos mean 0.00 - no measurable fitness effect in cell lines, which contrasts sharply with the published tumour-promoting claims.
key_refs: PMID:30531910 - Ma 2018 Nat Chem Biol: ZCCHC4 methylates 28S rRNA m6A4220 || PMID:31799605 - Pinto 2020 Nucleic Acids Res: independent confirmation of ZCCHC4 as 28S rRNA m6A MTase || PMID:35853866 - Zhu 2022 Signal Transduct Target Ther: ZCCHC4 promotes cancer chemoresistance
notes: 28S m6A4220 (sometimes numbered A4190/A4220 depending on reference); also reported to touch a small number of mRNAs. The flat DepMap profile makes it a good test case for context-dependent (e.g. drug-combination, 3D) dependency rather than fitness screening.

complex: MACOM (Hakai); E3-ligase-fold dimer that stabilises WTAP/VIRMA/ZC3H13
cancer_dependency_claims: Best known as the E-cadherin E3 ligase Hakai promoting EMT/invasion; direct m6A-linked cancer-dependency claims are limited. Local DepMap: NextGen class "Strongly Selective" (35 dependent lines), 2D Chronos mean -0.30 (14% of lines < -0.5) - selective, which is interesting given its biochemical role in complex stability.
key_refs: PMID:34145251 - Bawankar 2021 Nat Commun: Hakai/CBLL1 is a conserved MTC component required for stabilisation of core m6A machinery subunits
notes: Its ubiquitination (RING/HYB) activity is dispensable for m6A; the dimerisation/interaction surface is what is required, so it is a structural cofactor. Include as writer-cofactor but note that part of its phenotype is E-cadherin-related and m6A-independent.

complex: MAC (METTL3-METTL14 heterodimer) within the m6A-METTL complex
cancer_dependency_claims: METTL14 is required for AML cell self-renewal and blocks myeloid differentiation (high in MLL-rearranged/t(11q23) AML, MYB/MYC axis); it has been reported as both oncogenic (AML, glioma) and tumour-suppressive (HCC, colorectal) depending on context. Local DepMap: NextGen class "Pan-dependency", common-essential flag, 2D Chronos mean -0.56 (61% of lines < -0.5) - essentially the same profile as METTL3, as expected for an obligate heterodimer.
key_refs: PMID:24394384 - Wang 2014 Nat Cell Biol: METTL3/METTL14 act synergistically on m6A in mESCs || PMID:27281194 - Wang 2016 Nature: structural basis of m6A deposition by METTL3-METTL14 || PMID:29290617 - Weng 2017 Cell Stem Cell: METTL14 promotes leukaemogenesis
notes: Catalytically dead pseudo-MTase: it is an obligate structural/RNA-binding subunit (positively charged groove binds the substrate), hence writer-cofactor rather than writer. Its DepMap profile tracking METTL3 is a useful internal positive control for complex-level consistency.

complex: MACOM; SPEN-family paralogue that recruits WTAP/MAC to U-rich sites (e.g. XIST)
cancer_dependency_claims: RBM15 is the fusion partner in RBM15-MKL1 (OTT1-MAL) acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia, and RBM15-directed m6A on XIST/targets has been linked to leukaemic and breast-cancer phenotypes. Local DepMap: NextGen "High Variance" (55 dependent lines), 2D Chronos mean -0.21 (8% of lines < -0.5) - selective.
key_refs: PMID:27602518 - Patil 2016 Nature: RBM15/RBM15B recruit the m6A machinery to XIST for transcriptional silencing || PMID:29535189 - Knuckles 2018 Genes Dev: Rbm15/Spenito links to the m6A machinery via Zc3h13/Flacc
notes: Site-selection cofactor (binds U-rich motifs adjacent to methylation sites); redundant with RBM15B, so single-gene CRISPR effects are expected to be buffered - a paralog-buffering candidate in the NextGen paralog analysis.

complex: MACOM; RBM15 paralogue
cancer_dependency_claims: Few direct cancer-dependency claims; mainly implicated through redundancy with RBM15 in m6A site selection. Local DepMap: NextGen class "Non-dependency" (0 dependent lines), 2D Chronos mean -0.03 - essentially no single-gene dependency, consistent with RBM15/RBM15B redundancy.
key_refs: PMID:27602518 - Patil 2016 Nature: RBM15/RBM15B recruit the m6A machinery
notes: Include for completeness of MACOM; its flat profile makes the RBM15/RBM15B pair a good internal negative/paralog control.

complex: SERBP1-PCIF1 complex (reported to mediate m6Am deposition); SERBP1 also binds ribosomes/eEF1A independently
cancer_dependency_claims: No verified cancer-dependency claim for the m6Am function in this session; the published work is neuropathic pain/anxiety in mouse cortex. DepMap NextGen (local table): Pan-dependency, 86/147 NextGen and 55/108 organoid dependent lines - but SERBP1 has a large m6Am-independent role in translation/ribosome hibernation, so the dependency is almost certainly not m6Am-driven.
key_refs: PMID:40764612 - Huang 2025 Nat Commun: SERBP1 identified as a PCIF1 cofactor; the SERBP1-PCIF1 complex mediates m6Am deposition on Maf1 mRNA in glutamatergic neurons
notes: The only published obligate-ish partner proposed for PCIF1, and the catalog currently lists PCIF1 with no cofactor at all (unlike METTL3/METTL14 or RNMT/RAMAC). Tier 'proposed': one laboratory, mouse neurons, and the requirement for catalysis (versus targeting) is not firmly established - if the parent wants a strict obligate-cofactor bar, this is the entry to drop first.

complex: Obligate activating partner of METTL5 (18S m6A1832), BUD23/WBSCR22 (18S m7G1639), ALKBH8 (tRNA mcm5U) and N6AMT1/HEMK2 (protein/eRF1 methylation) | Obligate activator subunit shared by TRMT11, THUMPD3, TRMT9B?, BUD23, METTL5, ALKBH8 and others | obligate activator subunit of ALKBH8 and of BUD23, METTL5, HEMK2/N6AMT1, WBSCR22-family MTases | shared obligate activating subunit of BUD23, TRMT11, THUMPD3, THUMPD2, ALKBH8 (and the protein MTases METTL5, ALKBH8, N6AMT1/HEMK2)
cancer_dependency_claims: Not usually framed as a selective cancer target; it behaves as a housekeeping methyltransferase activator. Local DepMap: among the strongest dependencies in the whole dataset - Hart CEGv2 core essential, NextGen "Pan-dependency" in 147/147 lines, 2D Chronos mean -1.51 (95% of lines < -1), organoid mean -2.15. || Expected to be a strong, broadly essential hit because it activates several independent essential methyltransferases at once (ribosome biogenesis via BUD23 and METTL5, tRNA m2G via TRMT11/THUMPD3, U6 snRNA via THUMPD2). No single-cancer addiction claim; any DepMap signal is a convergent-cofactor signal, not evidence for one modification. || No gene-specific claim tied to wobble uridine; TRMT112 is a shared obligate cofactor whose dependency reflects several methyltransferase pathways at once (notably BUD23/18S m7G and METTL5/18S m6A). It is the single most essential gene in this scope in DepMap. || TRMT112 drives a growth- and metastasis-promoting program in triple-negative breast cancer (Elhamamsy 2026 Cell Death Differ); the THUMPD3-TRMT112 m2G complex promotes pancreatic cancer progression and autophagy via TFEB translation (Yuan 2026 Mol Cancer); pan-cancer analyses link it to the tumour microenvironment. DepMap (this project): median -2.04, 99.8% of models < -0.5, CEGv2 gene - near-ribosomal pan-essentiality.
key_refs: PMID:20123966 - interaction of ALKBH8 with the small accessory protein TRM112 is required to form a functional tRNA methyltransferase || PMID:25851604 - Zorbas 2015 Mol Biol Cell: WBSCR22-TRMT112 in human 18S rRNA methylation/ribosome biogenesis || PMID:31328227 - van Tran 2019 Nucleic Acids Res: TRMT112 stabilises and activates METTL5 || PMID:34669960 - Yang 2021 NAR: TRMT112 required to activate THUMPD3 for tRNA m2G6 || PMID:37283053 - Wang 2023 NAR: TRMT112 interactome in human cells; activates TRMT11, THUMPD3 and THUMPD2 as m2G MTases || PMID:41507361 - Elhamamsy 2026 Cell Death Differ, TRMT112 drives tumour growth and metastasis in TNBC || PMID:41530782 - Yuan 2026 Mol Cancer, THUMPD3-TRMT112 in pancreatic cancer || PMID:42689413 - Petrosyan 2026 NAR, TRMT112 is required for TRMT11 catalytic activity on mt-tRNAs
notes: Shared cofactor across several families (another curator will also list it). Its essentiality is driven mainly by BUD23-dependent ribosome biogenesis and eRF1/N6AMT1 methylation, not by 18S m6A - do not read a TRMT112 hit as evidence for m6A dependency. || The hub cofactor of this whole family - flag explicitly so that its dependency is not mis-assigned to any one mark. Will overlap with the m6A curator (METTL5) and the m5C/other curators. || CONFOUNDED by design: because TRMT112 partners with at least four unrelated MTases, a strong DepMap effect cannot be attributed to mcm5U. Overlaps with the m7G/m6A/m5C curators' lists. NextGen DepMap: Pan-dependency, 147/147 dependent lines, mean effect -2.15 (among the strongest in the genome). || Included because it is the obligate cofactor of the mitochondrial m2G10 writer TRMT11 (also overlaps the m7G/m5C/m6A curators' scopes). Its pan-essentiality is the sum of many methyltransferase partners, so it is uninformative as a single-mark dependency readout. || [review] CONFOUNDED BY DESIGN - do not attribute to any single mark. Obligate activator of BUD23 (18S m7G), METTL5 (18S m6A), TRMT11 and THUMPD3 (tRNA m2G), THUMPD2 (U6 m2G), ALKBH8 (mcm5U) and the protein MTase N6AMT1/HEMK2. Its near-maximal essentiality is the sum of these partners, and the TRMT112 (median ~-2.0, pan-essential) versus TRMT11 (median ~+0.13, non-essential) contrast is the cleanest internal proof of that point.

complex: MACOM; scaffold that bridges WTAP/HAKAI/ZC3H13 and directs 3'UTR / near-stop-codon methylation
cancer_dependency_claims: VIRMA/KIAA1429 is reported as an oncogenic driver in hepatocellular carcinoma (m6A-dependent GATA3 pre-mRNA regulation), breast, gastric and lung cancer. Local DepMap: NextGen "Pan-dependency" with the strongest effect of any MACOM subunit - 2D Chronos mean -0.79 (91% of lines < -0.5, 14% < -1), and strongly depleted in both 3D organoids (-1.15) and 2D (-1.13).
key_refs: PMID:29507755 - Yue 2018 Cell Discov: VIRMA mediates 3'UTR/stop-codon-proximal m6A and couples to APA || PMID:31856849 - Lan 2019 Mol Cancer: KIAA1429/VIRMA drives liver cancer via m6A-dependent GATA3 regulation
notes: Largest MACOM subunit; loss selectively removes 3'UTR m6A rather than all m6A, so it is a region-selective cofactor, not an obligate catalytic subunit. Its much stronger DepMap effect than METTL3 suggests m6A-independent essential functions (scaffolding/APA) - worth flagging in the user's analysis.

complex: MACOM (m6A-METTL-associated complex): WTAP-VIRMA-ZC3H13-CBLL1-RBM15/15B; recruits MAC to nuclear speckles/targets
cancer_dependency_claims: WTAP was described as an oncogenic protein in AML (stabilises/partners with WT1, promotes proliferation) and as an adverse prognostic factor in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and several solid tumours. Local DepMap: NextGen "Pan-dependency" and common-essential flag; 2D Chronos mean -0.46 (42% of lines < -0.5), slightly weaker than METTL3/14.
key_refs: PMID:24407421 - Ping 2014 Cell Res: WTAP is the regulatory subunit of the m6A methyltransferase || PMID:24413322 - Bansal 2014 Leukemia: WTAP is a novel oncogenic protein in AML || PMID:28454430 - Li 2017 Oncol Lett: WTAP as prognostic factor in PDAC
notes: Non-catalytic but required for nuclear localisation and target selection of MAC; WTAP loss phenocopies METTL3 loss for mRNA m6A. Also has splicing-regulator roles independent of m6A (Wilms-tumour-1-associated protein), so interpret dependency cautiously.

complex: MACOM; bridges RBM15/15B to WTAP and anchors the complex in the nucleus
cancer_dependency_claims: Mostly reported as a tumour suppressor (colorectal cancer, via Ras-ERK; low expression associated with poor prognosis), with oncogenic claims in a few settings. Local DepMap: NextGen class "High Variance" (69 dependent lines), not common-essential; 2D Chronos mean -0.29 with 11% of lines < -0.5 - a selective rather than pan dependency.
key_refs: PMID:29535189 - Knuckles 2018 Genes Dev: Zc3h13/Flacc bridges Rbm15 to Wtap in the m6A machinery || PMID:29547716 - Wen 2018 Mol Cell: Zc3h13 regulates nuclear m6A and mESC self-renewal
notes: Low-complexity nuclear scaffold; loss reduces but does not abolish m6A and causes cytoplasmic relocalisation of WTAP/VIRMA/HAKAI.

complex: eIF4F (EIF4E-EIF4G-EIF4A); regulated by 4E-BPs and MNK1/2; also binds RNMT
cancer_dependency_claims: eIF4E is a classical oncogene: copy gain/overexpression transforms cells, haploinsufficiency protects mice from Myc-driven lymphoma, and it is the node targeted by mTOR, MNK (eFT508/tomivosertib) and 4E/4G interaction inhibitors; ribavirin has been trialled as an eIF4E-directed agent in AML. Expected common essential in CRISPR screens.
key_refs: Marcotrigiano J 1997 Cell - crystal structure of eIF4E bound to 7-methyl-GDP defines m7G cap recognition by base sandwiching || PMID:35026230 - interaction between the cap maturation enzyme RNMT and the cap-binding protein eIF4E (J Mol Biol 2022)
notes: Included as the canonical cap-m7G reader: cap binding is strictly methylation-dependent (two stacked tryptophans read the positively charged m7G base), which satisfies the 'reader' definition. Its essentiality is translation-wide, so it is best used as a positive control for the cap module rather than as a candidate target discovered by the screen.

complex: 4EHP-GIGYF1/GIGYF2 repressor complex; also hypoxic eIF4F-alternative with HIF2A/RBM4
cancer_dependency_claims: Reported as a hypoxia-adaptation factor supporting cap-dependent translation when eIF4E is inhibited (HIF2A-eIF4E2 axis), suggesting context-selective dependency in hypoxic tumours; also a repressor arm with GIGYF2 whose loss increases translation of specific mRNAs. Not expected to be a common essential, so it is a good test of context-specific cap-reader dependency.
key_refs: Morita M 2012 Mol Cell Biol - 4EHP-GIGYF2 complex in translational repression || Rom E 1998 J Biol Chem - cloning and characterization of 4EHP, a cap-binding protein lacking eIF4G binding
notes: Genuine m7G-cap reader with much weaker cap affinity than eIF4E and no eIF4G binding; included for completeness of the cap-reader set.

complex: Nuclear cap-binding complex CBC (with NCBP1/CBP80)
cancer_dependency_claims: No modification-specific cancer claim; dependency arises from co-transcriptional RNA processing and export. Expected common essential in CRISPR screens.
key_refs: Calero G 2002 Nat Struct Biol - structural basis of m7GpppG recognition by the nuclear cap-binding complex || Mazza C 2002 EMBO J - crystal structure of the human nuclear cap-binding complex bound to m7GpppG
notes: The direct, methylation-dependent cap contact of the CBC (two tyrosines sandwich the m7G base). Together with EIF4E it is the best-characterised cap-m7G reader pair.

complex: QKI7 binds G3BP1 and partitions m7G-marked mRNAs into stress granules; STAR-family KH-domain RBP (dimer)
cancer_dependency_claims: QKI7 was reported to shuttle internal-m7G-marked transcripts into stress granules, attenuate translation of Hippo-pathway genes and thereby sensitise cancer cells to chemotherapy - i.e. QKI acts as a chemo-sensitivity modifier rather than a straightforward dependency (PMID:37379838). QKI is also a known tumour suppressor / fusion partner (e.g. MYB-QKI, NTRK-QKI) in other contexts, independent of m7G.
key_refs: PMID:37379838 - Zhao 2023 Cell: QKI proteins selectively recognise internal m7G (GANGAN motif) and shuttle those mRNAs into stress granules || PMID:39850560 - Zhou 2025 Front Pharmacol: review of METTL1/WDR4 and QKI as m7G-related enzymes in digestive disease
notes: Only proposed internal-m7G reader and so far essentially a single primary report; QKI has a long-established, large m7G-independent RBP function (myelination, splicing, circRNA), so DepMap signal will not be attributable to m7G reading.

complex: SNUPN-importin-beta (KPNB1) import receptor complex; released by RanBP1/CRM1
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer-dependency claim; the established human phenotype is biallelic SNUPN variants causing a recessive muscular dystrophy. Likely a moderate-to-strong CRISPR dependency via snRNP nuclear import, so expect a splicing-adjacent, non-selective signal.
key_refs: Huber J 1998 EMBO J - snurportin1, an m3G-cap-specific nuclear import receptor with a novel domain structure || PMID:15333938 - purification and crystallographic analysis of the m3G-cap-binding domain of human snurportin1 (Acta Crystallogr D 2004) || PMID:23885126 - Drosophila snurportin and importin-7 in snRNP biogenesis (Mol Biol Cell 2013)
notes: The cleanest true 'reader' in this whole scope: snurportin-1 binding is strictly dependent on the TMG (m2,2,7G) cap written by TGS1, with a dedicated m3G-cap-binding domain and a structurally defined recognition mode. Pairs with TGS1 for writer-reader epistasis tests.

complex: Nuclear cap-binding complex CBC (NCBP1/CBP80 + NCBP2/CBP20); links to ARS2/SRRT, PHAX, NEXT/CBCN
cancer_dependency_claims: No modification-specific cancer claim; CBC loss impairs splicing, snRNA export, nuclear RNA surveillance and NMD. Expected common essential in CRISPR screens, so treat as a positive control for the cap module.
key_refs: Izaurralde E 1994 Cell - a nuclear cap binding protein complex involved in pre-mRNA splicing || Mazza C 2002 EMBO J - crystal structure of the human nuclear cap-binding complex (CBP20-CBP80) with m7GpppG
notes: NCBP1/CBP80 does not itself contact the cap but is strictly required to fold NCBP2/CBP20 into its cap-binding conformation, hence reader-cofactor.

complex: BUD23-TRMT112
cancer_dependency_claims: Scores as a broadly essential ribosome-biogenesis gene: depletion blocks 18S-E pre-rRNA maturation and 40S production. Importantly, the 40S biogenesis requirement is catalysis-independent (a chaperone/quality-control function), so a methyltransferase inhibitor would likely NOT reproduce the CRISPR phenotype (PMID:25525153, PMID:25851604). Earlier work as 'MERM1' linked it to metastasis in breast cancer (Nakazawa 2011 - not verified here).
key_refs: PMID:25525153 - Haag 2015 RNA: WBSCR22/BUD23 mediates N7-methylation of G1639 in human 18S rRNA; catalytic activity dispensable for pre-rRNA processing || PMID:25851604 - Zorbas 2015 Mol Biol Cell: DIMT1L and WBSCR22-TRMT112 are required for ribosome biogenesis independently of their rRNA-modifying activity || PMID:37689068 - Liberman 2023 Mol Cell: BUD-23/BUD23 as the 18S m7G methyltransferase in an intergenerational-hormesis setting
notes: Current HGNC symbol is BUD23 (not WBSCR22). The catalysis-vs-scaffold split is the key interpretive caveat for any dependency analysis.

complex: METTL1-WDR4 (METTL1 = catalytic; WDR4 = obligate activating subunit)
cancer_dependency_claims: One of the best-supported RNA-modification oncogenic dependencies: METTL1 is amplified/overexpressed across cancers, its loss arrests the cell cycle and abolishes tumourigenicity, and overexpression alone transforms cells via increased m7G on Arg-TCT-4-1 tRNA and AGA-codon-biased translation (PMID:34352207); independently required for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma growth in vitro and in KO/overexpression mouse models (PMID:34352206). Further claims span lung, liver, colorectal, gastric, head-and-neck, glioma and thyroid cancer plus immune evasion (PMID:41562049).
key_refs: PMID:31031083 - Pandolfini 2019 Mol Cell: METTL1 m7G-methylates let-7e pri-miRNA and regulates miRNA processing/migration || PMID:34352206 - Dai 2021 Mol Cell: METTL1/WDR4 m7G tRNA modification promotes intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma || PMID:34352207 - Orellana 2021 Mol Cell: METTL1-mediated m7G on Arg-TCT tRNA drives oncogenic transformation
notes: Three substrate classes with decreasing confidence: internal tRNA m7G46 (core), miRNA (established, Kouzarides lab), internal mRNA m7G (established but lower stoichiometry; PMID:31031084). Prime candidate for the new DepMap - expect selective rather than pan-essential dependency.

complex: Obligate heterodimer RNMT-RAMAC; recruited to Pol II CTD (Ser5-P) and functionally coupled to CMTR1 | RNMT-RAMAC (RNMT-activating mini protein); also binds eIF4E
cancer_dependency_claims: MYC enhances cap methylation globally by recruiting RNMT and CDK7, raising cap methylation and translation of Wnt/beta-catenin transcripts (Mol Cancer Res 2017), and RNMT has been reported as required for MYC-driven lymphomagenesis - i.e. a MYC-cooperating rather than cell-autonomous-selective dependency. Small-molecule RNMT chemical probes are now being described (Biochem J 2025). Expected common essential in CRISPR screens. || Essential for gene expression generally, but with a reported synthetic-lethal-style selectivity: halving RNMT activity spared non-transformed mammary epithelial cells yet reduced proliferation and induced apoptosis in breast cancer lines, and sensitivity tracked oncogenic PIK3CA mutation (PI3Kalpha-dependent) (PMID:30991934). Also described as a MYC-supporting node (Cowling lab). Likely common-essential in DepMap, with PIK3CA status as a candidate modifier.
key_refs: PMID:22099306 - Gonatopoulos-Pournatzis 2011 Mol Cell: RNMT requires RAM for efficient cap methylation || PMID:22099306 - RAM/Fam103a1 is required for mRNA cap methylation (Mol Cell 2011) || PMID:27899423 - MYC mediates mRNA cap methylation of Wnt/beta-catenin transcripts by recruiting CDK7 and RNMT (Mol Cancer Res 2017) || PMID:30991934 - Dunn 2019 Open Biol: oncogenic PIK3CA mutations increase dependency on RNMT in breast cancer cells || PMID:35026230 - Osborne 2022 J Mol Biol: eIF4E directly binds the RNMT methyltransferase domain and competes with RAM || PMID:39869500 - characterisation of RNMT using a small-molecule approach (Biochem J 2025)
notes: Installs the cap N7-methyl on the cap guanosine (a cap-structure, not an internal nucleoside, modification). Strictly this is the m7G branch rather than Nm, but it is the same cap-maturation module as CMTR1/CMTR2 and PCIF1 and acts upstream of them, so it belongs in this scope. || Cap guanine-N7 methyltransferase (the m7G cap writer). Conceptually distinct from internal m7G - keep cap and internal m7G separate when interpreting dependency correlations.

complex: Interacts with SMN (recruitment to cytoplasmic snRNP assembly) and with Cajal-body machinery | recruited via SMN (survival of motor neuron) to cytoplasmic Sm-core snRNPs
cancer_dependency_claims: No strong direct cancer-dependency claim. The best-developed disease links are neuromuscular: TGS1 loss affects snRNA 3'-end processing and modulates SMN-dependent phenotypes (Nucleic Acids Res 2022). TGS1 also hypermethylates the telomerase RNA TERC cap and selenoprotein mRNA caps, giving indirect telomere- and redox-biology handles. Essentiality in CRISPR screens is intermediate/uncertain - worth checking rather than assuming. || No direct cancer dependency claim in this family's literature; TGS1 loss impairs snRNP nuclear import and, in model organisms, telomerase RNA capping and telomere homeostasis. Dependency, if any, is expected via splicing/snRNP biogenesis.
key_refs: Mouaikel 2002 Mol Cell - identification of Tgs1 as the snRNA/snoRNA cap trimethylguanosine synthase (yeast) || PMID:11983179 - hypermethylation of the cap of both snRNAs and snoRNAs requires the conserved nucleolar methyltransferase Tgs1 (Mol Cell 2002) || PMID:12776181 - Mouaikel 2003 EMBO Rep: human TGS1, the snRNA cap hypermethylase, interacts directly with SMN || PMID:12776181 - interaction between the snRNA cap hypermethylase TGS1 and the SMA protein SMN (EMBO Rep 2003) || PMID:35947650 - TGS1 impacts snRNA 3'-end processing and ameliorates SMN-dependent neurological phenotypes (Nucleic Acids Res 2022)
notes: Converts the m7G cap to 2,2,7-trimethylguanosine (TMG/m3G) on Sm-class snRNAs, box C/D and H/ACA snoRNAs, TERC and selenoprotein mRNAs. The TMG cap is the import signal read by SNUPN, so TGS1 and SNUPN form a true writer-reader pair within this scope. || Converts the m7G cap to 2,2,7-trimethylguanosine (TMG) on Sm-class snRNAs/snoRNAs and TERC - a guanine N2,N2 dimethylation on top of m7G, hence in scope for 'other base methylations'.

complex: Obligate activating subunit of RNMT (RNMT-RAMAC); also interacts with eIF4E | RNMT-RAMAC (RAMAC = obligate activating subunit; N-terminal RNMT-activating domain + C-terminal RNA-binding domain)
cancer_dependency_claims: No standalone cancer-dependency claim, but as the obligate activator of RNMT it should phenocopy RNMT and is expected to be a common essential in CRISPR screens. If the new DepMap shows RNMT and RAMAC co-dependency, that is a good internal positive control for the cap module. || No cancer-specific claim, but RAMAC is required for efficient cap methylation in vitro and in vivo, for maintaining mRNA levels and translation, and for cell viability (PMID:22099306) - i.e. expected common-essential and a co-dependency partner of RNMT.
key_refs: PMID:22099306 - Gonatopoulos-Pournatzis 2011 Mol Cell: RAM/Fam103a1 is required for mRNA cap methylation and cell viability || PMID:22099306 - RAM/Fam103a1 is required for mRNA cap methylation (Mol Cell 2011) || PMID:35026230 - interaction between the cap maturation enzyme RNMT and the cap-binding protein eIF4E (J Mol Biol 2022)
notes: Current HGNC symbol is RAMAC; FAM103A1 is the legacy symbol and is what appears in older annotation sets, so map carefully. Required for RNMT catalytic activation and for RNMT recruitment to transcription sites. || Current HGNC symbol is RAMAC (formerly FAM103A1/RAM). Correlated essentiality with RNMT is the expected signature.

complex: METTL1-WDR4 (WDR4 = non-catalytic, required for METTL1 activity)
cancer_dependency_claims: Phenocopies METTL1: up in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, correlates with poor prognosis, required for tumour cell survival and progression (PMID:34352206); Wdr4 KO mESCs lose self-renewal (PMID:29983320). Biallelic hypomorphic WDR4 mutations cause microcephalic primordial dwarfism (Galloway-Mowat/ tRNA-modification syndrome), so complete loss is likely broadly deleterious.
key_refs: PMID:29983320 - Lin 2018 Mol Cell: Mettl1/Wdr4 m7G tRNA methylome required for translation and ESC self-renewal || PMID:34352206 - Dai 2021 Mol Cell: WDR4 up in ICC and required for progression
notes: Obligate cofactor; treat its DepMap profile as a positive control for METTL1 (correlated essentiality is expected).

complex: Mitoribosome small-subunit late assembly factor carrying a [Fe4S4] cluster; Rsm22 homolog with a degenerate methyltransferase fold | binds the mitoribosomal small subunit during late assembly; harbours a [Fe4S4] cluster
cancer_dependency_claims: METTL17 is high in colorectal cancer and positively correlates with ferroptosis resistance; its depletion sensitises CRC cells to ferroptosis, impairs proliferation/migration/invasion, blocks xenograft and AOM/DSS tumourigenesis, and combined METTL17 loss + ferroptosis induction suppressed CRC xenografts (PMID:38377789). In that study METTL17 loss reduced multiple mitochondrial RNA methylations (m4C, m5C, m2G, m6A) simultaneously - consistent with an indirect, assembly-level effect. || METTL17 depletion sensitizes colorectal cancer cells to ferroptosis and impairs proliferation, migration, xenograft growth and AOM/DSS tumorigenesis, with reduced mitochondrial RNA methylation (m4C, m5C, m3C, m7G, m6A) reported as the mechanism (Li 2024 Redox Biol); bufalin is claimed to target METTL17 in oral cancer. DepMap (this project): median -0.37, 35% of models < -0.5 - one of the more broadly required genes in my scope.
key_refs: PMID:31487196 - Shi 2019 FASEB J, Mettl17 as a regulator of mt-rRNA modifications required for mitochondrial translation || PMID:31487196 - Shi 2019 FASEB J: Mettl17 loss reduces 12S mt-rRNA m4C840 (~70%) and m5C842 (~50%) and impairs mitochondrial translation || PMID:38199006 - Ast 2024 Mol Cell, METTL17 is an Fe-S cluster checkpoint for mitochondrial translation (assembly factor, no demonstrated RNA MTase activity) || PMID:38199006 - Ast 2024 Mol Cell: METTL17 is an Fe-S cluster checkpoint for mitochondrial translation; a late mitoribosome assembly factor, not shown to be a catalytic RNA MTase || PMID:38377789 - Li 2024 Redox Biol, METTL17 coordinates ferroptosis and tumorigenesis in colorectal cancer || PMID:38377789 - Li 2024 Redox Biol: METTL17 coordinates ferroptosis and tumorigenesis via mitochondrial translation in CRC
notes: Assigned role 'other' and tier 'controversial' deliberately: METTL17 is a SAM-binding, 7BS-fold protein whose effects on 12S mt-rRNA m4C/m5C are most parsimoniously explained by its role as an Fe-S-dependent assembly chaperone (METTL15 makes m4C840; NSUN4 makes m5C842). Treat it as an RWE-adjacent assembly factor, not a validated writer. It is nonetheless one of the more interesting cancer-dependency candidates in this list. || Classified role 'other' deliberately: no RNA methyltransferase activity has ever been demonstrated for human METTL17, and cryo-EM/biochemistry support an Fe-S-dependent assembly-checkpoint function. Keep it in the catalog (it is widely listed as a writer) but flag the assignment as controversial; its dependency likely reflects mitoribosome assembly and Fe-S status (e.g. FXN-deficient contexts).

complex: none known
cancer_dependency_claims: No cancer dependency claims. In the local DepMap NextGen tables NSUN7 is a Non-dependency with 0 dependent lines in both panels. Expression is largely testis-restricted.
key_refs: Aguilo 2016 Cell Reports - earlier proposal that NSUN7 methylates enhancer RNAs including at the PGC1A locus || PMID:41381527 - NSUN7 is a catalytically INACTIVE RNA m5C methyltransferase: Nsun7 knockout does not change RNA m5C, motif IV Asp is replaced by Leu abolishing SAM binding; required non-catalytically for sperm flagellum assembly
notes: Important 2025 correction: although NSUN7 carries motifs IV and VI, it cannot bind SAM and is not an m5C writer - the earlier enhancer-RNA methylation claim is not supported. Keep it in the catalogue as a family member/negative control, not as a writer. Human variants cause male infertility.

cancer_dependency_claims: Acts as a tumour-promoting gene in breast cancer in the loss-of-function direction: BCDIN3D depletion raises mature miR-145 and suppresses tumorigenic phenotypes of breast cancer cells (PMID:23063121), and BCDIN3D loss reduces glycolytic capacity via let-7-dependent downregulation of ALDOC (PMID:33664453). So a candidate selective dependency in breast cancer, plus an obesity/T2D locus link.
key_refs: PMID:23063121 - Xhemalce 2012 Cell: BCDIN3D O-methylates the 5'-monophosphate of pre-miR-145, reducing Dicer processing || PMID:33664453 - Reinsborough 2021 Oncogene: BCDIN3D stimulates ALDOC expression and glycolysis through let-7 in breast cancer cells
notes: FLAG AS NON-NUCLEOSIDE, as instructed: BCDIN3D phospho-dimethylates the 5'-terminal monophosphate of pre-miRNAs (and tRNA-His), not a base or ribose. Keep it separate from nucleoside-modification analyses; same family as MEPCE.

complex: 7SK snRNP core with LARP7, HEXIM1/HEXIM2 and P-TEFb (CDK9/CCNT1) | 7SK snRNP with LARP7, HEXIM1/2 and P-TEFb (CDK9/CCNT1)
cancer_dependency_claims: No modification-specific cancer claim. Mechanistically relevant to transcription-addicted cancers: MEPCE loss destabilises 7SK and releases active P-TEFb/CDK9, so MEPCE-depleted cells show increased pause release - the opposite polarity of CDK9 inhibitors. Expected to score as a dependency in many lines via 7SK/P-TEFb homeostasis rather than via a nucleoside mark. || No m7G/base-methylation-based cancer claim; MEPCE is a P-TEFb sequestration factor and its loss de-represses CDK9, which has been linked to transcriptional addiction in MYC-driven tumours. Any dependency signal reflects 7SK snRNP integrity, not nucleoside methylation.
key_refs: Jeronimo C 2007 Mol Cell - systematic analysis of the human 7SK snRNP identifies MEPCE as the methylphosphate capping enzyme || PMID:17643375 - Jeronimo 2007 Mol Cell: BCDIN3/MEPCE identified as the 7SK snRNA methylphosphate capping enzyme within a P-TEFb-containing snRNP || PMID:35320752 - structural basis of RNA conformational switching in the transcriptional regulator 7SK RNP (Mol Cell 2022)
notes: FLAG as requested: MEPCE installs a gamma-monomethyl phosphate cap on the 5' end of 7SK (and U6), which is a terminal phosphate methylation, NOT a modified nucleoside. Keep it in the catalog for completeness but exclude it from any 'modified nucleoside' aggregate score. || FLAG AS NON-NUCLEOSIDE: MEPCE methylates the gamma-phosphate of the 5'-end (monomethyl phosphate cap), not a base or ribose. Included for completeness of the 'guanine/phosphate methylation' space and because 7SK is in scope; exclude it if the analysis is restricted to modified nucleosides.

complex: Standalone radical-SAM Fe-S methylthiotransferase acting after TRIT1 on mt-tRNA A37 (Phe, Ser(UCN), Trp, Tyr)
cancer_dependency_claims: CDK5RAP1-mediated ms2 conversion promotes maintenance of glioma-initiating cells (Yamamoto 2019 iScience); earlier work reported that CDK5RAP1 knockdown causes ROS/JNK-dependent cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis in breast cancer cells and NF-kB-linked apoptosis in A375 melanoma. DepMap (this project): median +0.10, 0.2% of models < -0.5 - no broad dependency.
key_refs: PMID:22422838 - Reiter 2012 NAR, CDK5RAP1 is a methylthiotransferase acting on nuclear and mitochondrial RNA || PMID:25738458 - Wei 2015 Cell Metab, Cdk5rap1-mediated ms2 modification of mt-tRNAs, translation and myopathy || PMID:31654853 - Yamamoto 2019 iScience, CDK5RAP1 ms2 conversion maintains glioma-initiating cells
notes: Fakruddin 2017 NAR showed the ms2 mark is confined to mitochondria-encoded RNAs, correcting earlier claims of nuclear-derived ms2i6A substrates. Fe-S dependent, so its profile may track FXN/ISC genes.

complex: Standalone radical-SAM methylthiotransferase (MTTase) with Fe-S clusters; acts after t6A37 on cytoplasmic tRNA-Lys(UUU)
cancer_dependency_claims: CDKAL1 is required to maintain cancer stem-like cells in rhabdomyosarcoma and several common cancers, but via a catalysis-independent N-terminal function that assembles the eIF4F initiation complex to translate SALL2 (Huang 2023 Adv Sci); osimertinib was later reported to block MYLK4-mediated CDKAL1 phosphorylation, suppressing RMS stemness/chemoresistance (Itano 2026 Signal Transduct Target Ther). DepMap (this project): median +0.11, 0.9% of models < -0.5 (a few strong outliers to -1.66).
key_refs: PMID:20584901 - Arragain 2010 JBC, identification of CDKAL1 as the ms2t6A methylthiotransferase || PMID:21841312 - Wei 2011 JCI, Cdkal1 loss, tRNA-Lys hypomodification and type 2 diabetes || PMID:36786012 - Huang 2023 Adv Sci, CDKAL1 maintains cancer stem-like cells via eIF4F
notes: Best known as a type 2 diabetes GWAS gene. Importantly, the cancer-stemness claim is explicitly NOT dependent on its tRNA-modifying activity, so a DepMap hit would not validate ms2t6A as the mechanism.

complex: Standalone leucine-carboxyl-methyltransferase-family enzyme performing the final methoxycarbonylation/methylation step of yW
cancer_dependency_claims: OHyW and LCMT2/TYW4 levels fall in AML relative to MDS; low LCMT2 correlates with reduced drug sensitivity and limited differentiation capacity in AML lines, and the authors propose targeting LCMT2 to improve therapy (Chen 2025 Br J Haematol). Frameshift mutations in LCMT2 repeat sequences have been reported in MSI colon cancers. DepMap (this project): median +0.05, 0.7% of models < -0.5.
key_refs: PMID:16642040 - Noma 2006 EMBO J, TYW4 completes wybutosine synthesis || PMID:39523586 - Chen 2025 Br J Haematol, hydroxy-wybutosine/LCMT2(TYW4) in MDS-to-AML progression
notes: Named LCMT2 in HGNC with TYW4 only an alias - a common source of gene-list misses. Note the AML claim is a loss-of-mark biomarker claim, not a fitness dependency.

complex: KEOPS/EKC (OSGEP-TP53RK-TPRKB-LAGE3-GON7); catalytic subunit
cancer_dependency_claims: OSGEP loss in melanoma disrupts ANN-codon translation, causes protein aggregation and stress granules that relocalize RIG-I, triggering an anti-tumour T-cell response and tumour regression; an OSGEP-driven signature tracks with T-cell infiltration and survival (Dziagwa 2026 Nat Commun), framing t6A as a melanoma immuno-oncology target. Also reported as an N-CoR-cleaving protease in AML-M5. DepMap (this project, n=1,208): median -1.53, 97% of models < -0.5, CEGv2 gene.
key_refs: PMID:28805828 - Braun 2017 Nat Genet, KEOPS-complex mutations cause nephrotic syndrome with microcephaly || PMID:35104889 - Wang 2022 NAR, tRNA substrate recognition by eukaryotic KEOPS || PMID:41735308 - Dziagwa 2026 Nat Commun, OSGEP loss triggers RIG-I anti-tumour immunity in melanoma
notes: Kae1 homolog; catalysis absolutely requires the other KEOPS subunits plus YRDC-generated TC-AMP. Strongly common-essential in DepMap.

complex: Acts as a homodimer with YRDC-generated TC-AMP; no KEOPS subunits required (mitochondrial Qri7-type enzyme)
cancer_dependency_claims: Weak: a TCGA/multi-omics paper calls OSGEPL1 an HCC oncogene correlated with grade/stage and worse survival (Mui 2025 Discov Oncol); no CRISPR-based dependency claim. DepMap (this project): median +0.13, 0% of models < -0.5 - among the most clearly dispensable genes in this family, consistent with mt-translation enzymes being conditionally rather than absolutely required in 2D glucose culture.
key_refs: PMID:29760464 - Lin 2018 Nat Commun, CO2/bicarbonate-sensitive mt t6A37 by YRDC and OSGEPL1 || PMID:32047918 - Zhou 2020 NAR, molecular basis for t6A modification in human mitochondria || PMID:38227555 - Zhang 2024 NAR, t6A biogenesis in efficiency and fidelity of mitochondrial gene expression
notes: mt-t6A37 is dynamically tuned by intracellular CO2/bicarbonate - a metabolic-sensing link that could make OSGEPL1 dependency media- or 3D/organoid-context dependent, which is directly relevant to the NextGen 3D DepMap.

complex: Standalone RNA galactosyltransferase acting on Q34 of tRNA-Tyr (UDP-Gal donor)
cancer_dependency_claims: None. Zebrafish qtgal knockouts show shortened body length; no cancer dependency reported. DepMap (this project): median +0.17, 0.1% of models < -0.5.
key_refs: PMID:37992713 - Zhao 2023 Cell, biochemical identification of QTGAL and QTMAN as RNA glycosylases forming galQ/manQ || PMID:40899493 - Pichler 2025 Angew Chem, selective chemical manipulation of manQ/galQ in tRNAs of living cells
notes: Newly named gene (HGNC symbol changed from B3GNTL1 to QTGAL in 2025) - a 2023-2025 addition that most RWE gene lists still miss. galQ suppresses stop-codon readthrough; loss increases protein aggregation.

complex: Standalone RNA mannosyltransferase acting on Q34 of tRNA-Asp (GDP-Man donor)
cancer_dependency_claims: None reported. DepMap (this project): median +0.25, 0% of models < -0.5 - the single most dispensable gene in my scope.
key_refs: PMID:37992713 - Zhao 2023 Cell, QTMAN reconstitutes manQ on tRNA-Asp; ribosome profiling of knockouts || PMID:40899493 - Pichler 2025 Angew Chem, chemical manipulation of manQ/galQ
notes: HGNC symbol changed from GTDC1 to QTMAN in 2025. Cryo-EM in Zhao 2023 explains how Q-glycosylation tunes codon recognition; vertebrate-specific.

complex: Eukaryotic tRNA-guanine transglycosylase (TGT) heterodimer QTRT1 (catalytic) - QTRT2 (accessory)
cancer_dependency_claims: QTRT1 knockout/knockdown reduced proliferation and migration of MCF7/MDA-MB-231 cells and altered xenograft growth and tumour microbiome recruitment (Zhang 2020 Cancers); high QTRT1 predicts poor prognosis in lung adenocarcinoma. Q-tRNA levels also gate proliferation and MHC-II expression, and the microbial precursor preQ1 competes with queuine to repress proliferation and suppress tumour growth in mice (Zhang 2025 Nat Cell Biol). DepMap (this project): median +0.04, 0.4% of models < -0.5 - dispensable in standard media (expected, since Q depends on exogenous queuine).
key_refs: PMID:20354154 - Chen 2010 RNA, human TGT is a QTRT1-QTRT2 heterodimer || PMID:30093495 - Tuorto 2018 EMBO J, queuosine-modified tRNAs confer nutritional control of translation || PMID:32182756 - Zhang 2020 Cancers, QTRT1 modulates growth and microbiome recruitment to breast tumours
notes: Diet/microbiome-dependent substrate (queuine) means DepMap medium composition largely determines whether this pathway is even active - a strong reason to check the NextGen serum/medium covariates before interpreting any Q-pathway effect.

complex: Standalone dimethylallyltransferase; acts on A37 of a limited substrate set including tRNA-Ser(Sec)
cancer_dependency_claims: Historically a candidate lung tumour suppressor (reduced expression in lung adenocarcinoma, growth-suppressive on re-expression; Spinola 2005 Oncogene). Opposite direction in SCLC: gene-amplification-driven TRIT1 overexpression confers sensitivity to arsenic trioxide (Coll-SanMartin 2021 Cancers). In HCC, TRIT1 ablation blocks selenoprotein (GPX4 pathway) synthesis and induces ferroptosis downstream of the mevalonate/IPP supply (Chen 2025 J Hepatol). DepMap (this project): median -0.15, 15% of models < -0.5 with a long tail to -2.81 - a selective rather than common dependency.
key_refs: PMID:24901367 - Yarham 2014 PLoS Genet, pathogenic TRIT1 mutations cause defective i6A37 in mitochondrial and cytosolic tRNAs || PMID:33919717 - Coll-SanMartin 2021 Cancers, TRIT1 amplification/overexpression and arsenic trioxide sensitivity in SCLC || PMID:40653112 - Chen 2025 J Hepatol, TRIT1-dependent Sec-tRNA modification and ferroptosis in liver cancer
notes: IPP (mevalonate pathway) is the isopentenyl donor, so TRIT1 dependency should covary with mevalonate-pathway and selenoprotein dependencies - a good co-dependency test in DepMap. Dual cytosolic/mitochondrial.

complex: Standalone class VIII (single-sheeted beta-barrel, UPF0066) AdoMet methyltransferase
cancer_dependency_claims: None specific. TRMO appears only inside multi-gene 'tRNA modification regulator' prognostic signatures (e.g. clear-cell renal carcinoma), which are not dependency evidence. DepMap (this project): median +0.20, 0.2% of models < -0.5 - dispensable.
key_refs: PMID:25063302 - Kimura 2014 NAR, discovery of TrmO/TRMO; recombinant human TRMO methylates t6A37 to m6t6A in tRNA-Ser(GCU) || PMID:41654963 - Cuper 2026 Biol Res, tissue-specific role of Drosophila dTrmO in threonine decoding
notes: Human assignment rests on recombinant-enzyme reconstitution plus detection of m6t6A37 (~56% occupancy) in HeLa cytoplasmic tRNA-Ser(GCU); no human knockout phenotype published, hence 'established' not 'core'. Unlike bacteria, mammals lack ct6A, so TRMO competes with no TcdA.

complex: Standalone radical-SAM flavoenzyme (4-demethylwyosine synthase); second step of the yW pathway after TRMT5-made m1G37
cancer_dependency_claims: No specific dependency claim; TYW1 appears in a report that yW hypomodification activates HERVK and impairs neuronal differentiation (Sun 2024 iScience). DepMap (this project): median +0.11, 0.5% of models < -0.5.
key_refs: PMID:16642040 - Noma 2006 EMBO J, biosynthesis of wybutosine defines TYW1-TYW4 || PMID:34184886 - Young 2021 Biochemistry, eukaryotic TYW1 is a radical SAM flavoenzyme || PMID:36326713 - Young 2022 Biochemistry, imidazoline ring formation entails oxidative cleavage of pyruvate
notes: Fe-S/flavin enzyme using pyruvate as the C-C donor. Step order: TRMT5 (m1G37) -> TYW1 -> TYW2 -> TYW3 -> LCMT2(TYW4) -> TYW5 (hydroxylation to OHyW).

complex: Paralog of TYW1 (7q11.23 segmental duplication region)
cancer_dependency_claims: None. DepMap (this project): data in only 381/1,208 models (median -0.03), consistent with poor/ambiguous guide mapping in the duplicated 7q11.23 interval.
key_refs: PMID:16642040 - Noma 2006 EMBO J, yW pathway defining TYW1 activity (paralog by homology)
notes: Function inferred from homology only; HGNC has carried it as both a protein-coding paralog and LINC00069. Guides may cross-target TYW1 - treat any DepMap signal here with caution and check guide multiplicity.

complex: Standalone alpha-amino-alpha-carboxypropyl transferase (third step of yW pathway)
cancer_dependency_claims: Two distinct and opposite-direction claims. (1) Oncogenic/amplified: TRMT12 is amplified and overexpressed in breast cancer and overexpression independently predicts poor survival in HNSCC. (2) Tumour-suppressive/immunological: promoter-hypermethylation silencing of TYW2 in colorectal cancer causes -1 ribosome frameshifts, ROBO1 decay, EMT and worse early-stage survival (Rossello-Tortella 2020 PNAS); TYW2 knockout generates immunogenic out-of-frame peptides, increases tumour immunogenicity and sensitizes to anti-PD-1, and low TYW2 associates with checkpoint-blockade response in patients (Weller 2025 Cancer Cell). DepMap (this project): median +0.03, 1.7% of models < -0.5 (tail to -2.77).
key_refs: PMID:17440925 - Rodriguez 2007 Genes Chromosomes Cancer, TRMT12 amplification/overexpression in breast cancer || PMID:32778592 - Rossello-Tortella 2020 PNAS, epigenetic loss of TYW2 induces ribosome frameshifts in colon cancer || PMID:40154482 - Weller 2025 Cancer Cell, TYW2 loss yields targetable antigens and anti-PD-1 sensitivity
notes: IMPORTANT NOMENCLATURE: HGNC approved symbol is now TYW2 (changed from TRMT12 on 2025-06-16). Most pre-2025 cancer literature and many gene lists use TRMT12. Because loss (not gain) drives immunogenicity, TYW2 is a candidate anti-dependency/immune-sensitizing gene rather than a fitness gene.

complex: Standalone SAM-dependent methyltransferase (TYW3/Taw3 class); fourth step of yW pathway
cancer_dependency_claims: None. DepMap (this project): median +0.14, 0.1% of models < -0.5.
key_refs: PMID:16642040 - Noma 2006 EMBO J, yW pathway assignment of TYW3 || PMID:27932585 - Currie 2017 RNA, structural and functional characterization of the TYW3/Taw3 class of SAM-dependent methyltransferases
notes: Human enzymology is largely inferred from yeast Taw3 and archaeal structures plus the Noma pathway reconstruction - solid but less directly demonstrated in human cells than TYW1/TYW2.

complex: Standalone Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate JmjC-domain RNA hydroxylase (makes OHyW from yW)
cancer_dependency_claims: None in cancer; TYW5 is mainly discussed as a schizophrenia risk gene via distal regulatory variants at 2q33.1. DepMap (this project): median +0.13, 0.3% of models < -0.5.
key_refs: PMID:20739293 - Noma 2010 JBC, expanding the role of the JmjC domain as an RNA hydroxylase (TYW5) || PMID:20972222 - Kato 2011 NAR, crystal structure of TYW5
notes: First JmjC protein shown to hydroxylate RNA rather than protein; 2-OG dependent, so potentially sensitive to oncometabolite (2-HG) inhibition - an untested but testable IDH-mutant context.

complex: TC-AMP-forming enzyme acting upstream of KEOPS (OSGEP/TP53RK/TPRKB/LAGE3/GON7) in the cytosol and of OSGEPL1 in mitochondria
cancer_dependency_claims: Top essential tRNA-modification enzyme in a CRISPR screen in glioblastoma stem cells; threonine accumulation feeds YRDC-dependent t6A and codon-biased (ANN) translation, and dietary threonine restriction reduces tumour t6A and growth (Wu 2024 Nat Cancer); targeting YRDC blocks codon-biased FABP7 translation and overcomes GBM chemoresistance (Zhang 2026 Oncogene). Upregulated in NSCLC with knockdown anti-proliferative. Pan-essential in DepMap: in the post-26Q1 Chronos matrix in this project (n=1,208 models) median gene effect -2.35, 88% of models < -0.5, and it is a Hart CEGv2 core-essential gene.
key_refs: PMID:23620299 - Wan 2013 NAR, reconstitution of eukaryotic t6A with YRDC + KEOPS || PMID:31481669 - Arrondel 2019 Nat Commun, YRDC and GON7 mutations cause Galloway-Mowat syndrome || PMID:38519786 - Wu 2024 Nat Cancer, YRDC/threonine codon-biased translation in GSCs
notes: Bifunctional/dual-compartment: supplies threonylcarbamoyl-AMP for both cytosolic (KEOPS) and mitochondrial (OSGEPL1) t6A37. Essentiality in DepMap is near-ribosomal in magnitude, so any cancer-selective signal must be assessed against a common-essential background.

complex: KEOPS/EKC; fifth core subunit (yeast Gon7 homolog), binds LAGE3/Pcc1
cancer_dependency_claims: No credible cancer-dependency claim; the literature is human-genetics (Galloway-Mowat syndrome with YRDC) and structural. DepMap (this project): median +0.06, 0.4% of models < -0.5 - non-essential.
key_refs: PMID:27903914 - Wan 2017 NAR, proteomics identifies C14ORF142 as core KEOPS subunit homologous to yeast Gon7 || PMID:31481669 - Arrondel 2019 Nat Commun, GON7 mutations and t6A defects in Galloway-Mowat syndrome || PMID:34614169 - Beenstock 2021 NAR, structural and functional workings of KEOPS
notes: Intrinsically disordered; current HGNC symbol GON7 (changed from C14orf142 in 2016). Its non-essentiality in CRISPR data contrasts with KEOPS obligacy claims in vitro.

complex: KEOPS/EKC; Pcc1 homolog, mediates KEOPS dimerization
cancer_dependency_claims: Mostly correlative/overexpression biology rather than a dependency: LAGE3 is reported to promote metastasis and stemness in NSCLC via AKT/PI3K, to stabilize VEGFA mRNA and drive angiogenesis in HCC, and to associate with poor prognosis in HCC and colorectal cancer. DepMap (this project): median -0.08, only 5% of models < -0.5 - essentially non-essential, which is notable given its obligate role in KEOPS.
key_refs: PMID:27302132 - Wan 2016 NAR, Pcc1/LAGE3-mediated KEOPS dimerization in t6A biosynthesis || PMID:28805828 - Braun 2017 Nat Genet, LAGE3 among KEOPS disease genes || PMID:38653358 - Cong 2024 BBA Mol Basis Dis, LAGE3 stabilizes VEGFA mRNA in HCC
notes: X-linked. The flat DepMap profile versus strong OSGEP/YRDC essentiality suggests either functional buffering or incomplete knockout sensitivity - a useful internal control in the analysis.

complex: TGT heterodimer with QTRT1; non-catalytic but obligate subunit (also provides outer-mitochondrial-membrane anchoring)
cancer_dependency_claims: No direct cancer-dependency claim; implicated with QTRT1 in Q-dependent codon-biased elongation (learning/memory, inflammatory bowel disease) and required for mitochondrial Q34. DepMap (this project): median +0.15, 0.2% of models < -0.5.
key_refs: PMID:32859890 - Suzuki 2020 Nat Commun, QTRT1 and QTRT2 are both required for Q34 in mt-tRNAs || PMID:34241577 - Sievers 2021 RNA Biol, structural and functional insights into human TGT || PMID:37609797 - Cirzi 2023 EMBO J, Q-tRNA and codon-biased translation elongation speed
notes: Current HGNC symbol QTRT2 (renamed from QTRTD1 in 2016); still frequently published as QTRTD1.

complex: KEOPS/EKC; atypical protein kinase (Bud32) subunit required for OSGEP activity
cancer_dependency_claims: PRPK/TP53RK confers poor prognosis and is a proposed target in multiple myeloma (Hideshima 2017 Blood); identified in a kinase-focused CRISPR screen as a regulator of colorectal cancer survival acting through CDC7/MCM-dependent replication, p53-independently (Choi 2025 Sci Rep); PRPK/TOPK co-targeting proposed for skin cancer. DepMap (this project): median -0.65 with 73% of models < -0.5 but only 12% < -1 - a broad, moderate dependency rather than a hard common essential.
key_refs: PMID:28082445 - Hideshima 2017 Blood, PRPK in multiple myeloma || PMID:33547416 - Li 2021 Commun Biol, crystal structure of human PRPK-TPRKB || PMID:41102525 - Choi 2025 Sci Rep, TP53RK in colorectal cancer survival
notes: Kinase activity and the TPRKB interaction are both needed for efficient t6A; several cancer papers invoke non-t6A substrates (p53 Ser15, CDC7), so a t6A-independent dependency component is plausible.

complex: KEOPS/EKC; Cgi121 subunit, binds TP53RK and contributes to tRNA recruitment
cancer_dependency_claims: In shRNA screening data TPRKB was the most significant vulnerability of TP53-mutant/MDM2-amplified cancer lines, and knockdown inhibited proliferation selectively in TP53-deficient cells in vitro and in vivo while depletion of other KEOPS subunits behaved p53-independently (Goswami 2019 Mol Cancer Res) - i.e. an explicitly genotype-selective KEOPS dependency claim worth testing in a larger DepMap. DepMap (this project): median -0.44, 44% of models < -0.5.

notes: Cgi121 homolog; non-catalytic. The TP53-selective claim is the single most directly DepMap-testable hypothesis in this family.
